22.he: אָמַ֣ר עָ֭צֵל אֲרִ֣י בַח֑וּץ בְּת֥וֹךְ רְ֝חֹב֗וֹת אֵֽרָצֵֽחַ׃

lines.text: The sluggard says, “There is a lion outside! I will be killed in the streets!”
The slothful hath said, 'A lion [is] without, In the midst of the broad places I am slain.'

22.he: שׁוּחָ֣ה עֲ֭מֻקָּה פִּ֣י זָר֑וֹת זְע֥וּם יְ֝הוָ֗ה יפול־שָֽׁם׃

lines.text: The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit. He who is under Yahweh’s wrath will fall into it.
A deep pit [is] the mouth of strange women, The abhorred of Jehovah falleth there.

22.he: אִ֭וֶּלֶת קְשׁוּרָ֣ה בְלֶב־נָ֑עַר שֵׁ֥בֶט מ֝וּסָ֗ר יַרְחִיקֶ֥נָּה מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

lines.text: Folly is bound up in the heart of a child: the rod of discipline drives it far from him.
Folly is bound up in the heart of a youth, The rod of chastisement putteth it far from him.

22.he: עֹ֣שֵֽׁק דָּ֭ל לְהַרְבּ֣וֹת ל֑וֹ נֹתֵ֥ן לְ֝עָשִׁ֗יר אַךְ־לְמַחְסֽוֹר׃

lines.text: Whoever oppresses the poor for his own increase and whoever gives to the rich, both come to poverty.
He is oppressing the poor to multiply to him, He is giving to the rich — only to want.

22.he: הַ֥ט אָזְנְךָ֗ וּ֭שְׁמַע דִּבְרֵ֣י חֲכָמִ֑ים וְ֝לִבְּךָ֗ תָּשִׁ֥ית לְדַעְתִּֽי׃

lines.text: Turn your ear, and listen to the words of the wise. Apply your heart to my teaching.
Incline thine ear, and hear words of the wise, And thy heart set to my knowledge,

22.he: כִּֽי־נָ֭עִים כִּֽי־תִשְׁמְרֵ֣ם בְּבִטְנֶ֑ךָ יִכֹּ֥נוּ יַ֝חְדָּ֗ו עַל־שְׂפָתֶֽיךָ׃

lines.text: For it is a pleasant thing if you keep them within you, if all of them are ready on your lips.
For they are pleasant when thou dost keep them in thy heart, They are prepared together for thy lips.

22.he: לִהְי֣וֹת בַּ֭יהוָה מִבְטַחֶ֑ךָ הוֹדַעְתִּ֖יךָ הַיּ֣וֹם אַף־אָֽתָּה׃

lines.text: I teach you today, even you, So that your trust may be in Yahweh.
That thy trust may be in Jehovah, I caused thee to know to-day, even thou.

22.he: הֲלֹ֤א כָתַ֣בְתִּי לְ֭ךָ שלשום בְּמ֖וֹעֵצֹ֣ת וָדָֽעַת׃

lines.text: Haven’t I written to you thirty excellent things of counsel and knowledge,
Have I not written to thee three times With counsels and knowledge?

22.he: לְהוֹדִֽיעֲךָ֗ קֹ֭שְׁטְ אִמְרֵ֣י אֱמֶ֑ת לְהָשִׁ֥יב אֲמָרִ֥ים אֱ֝מֶ֗ת לְשֹׁלְחֶֽיךָ׃

lines.text: To teach you truth, reliable words, to give sound answers to the ones who sent you?
To cause thee to know the certainty of sayings of truth, To return sayings of truth to those sending thee.

22.he: אַֽל־תִּגְזָל־דָּ֭ל כִּ֣י דַל־ה֑וּא וְאַל־תְּדַכֵּ֖א עָנִ֣י בַשָּֽׁעַר׃

lines.text: Don’t exploit the poor, because he is poor; and don’t crush the needy in court;
Rob not the poor because he [is] poor, And bruise not the afflicted in the gate.

22.he: כִּֽי־יְ֭הוָה יָרִ֣יב רִיבָ֑ם וְקָבַ֖ע אֶת־קֹבְעֵיהֶ֣ם נָֽפֶשׁ׃

lines.text: for Yahweh will plead their case, and plunder the life of those who plunder them.
For Jehovah pleadeth their cause, And hath spoiled the soul of their spoilers.

22.he: אַל־תִּ֭תְרַע אֶת־בַּ֣עַל אָ֑ף וְאֶת־אִ֥ישׁ חֵ֝מוֹת לֹ֣א תָבֽוֹא׃

lines.text: Don’t befriend a hot-tempered man, and don’t associate with one who harbors anger:
Shew not thyself friendly with an angry man, And with a man of fury go not in,

22.he: פֶּן־תֶּאֱלַ֥ף ארחתו וְלָקַחְתָּ֖ מוֹקֵ֣שׁ לְנַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃

lines.text: lest you learn his ways, and ensnare your soul.
Lest thou learn his paths, And have received a snare to thy soul.

22.he: אַל־תְּהִ֥י בְתֹֽקְעֵי־כָ֑ף בַּ֝עֹרְבִ֗ים מַשָּׁאֽוֹת׃

lines.text: Don’t you be one of those who strike hands, of those who are collateral for debts.
Be not thou among those striking hands, Among sureties [for] burdens.

22.he: אִם־אֵֽין־לְךָ֥ לְשַׁלֵּ֑ם לָ֥מָּה יִקַּ֥ח מִ֝שְׁכָּבְךָ֗ מִתַּחְתֶּֽיךָ׃

lines.text: If you don’t have means to pay, why should he take away your bed from under you?
If thou hast nothing to pay, Why doth he take thy bed from under thee?

22.he: אַל־תַּ֭סֵּג גְּב֣וּל עוֹלָ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר עָשׂ֣וּ אֲבוֹתֶֽיךָ׃

lines.text: Don’t move the ancient boundary stone which your fathers have set up.
Remove not a border of olden times, That thy fathers have made.

22.he: חָזִ֡יתָ אִ֤ישׁ ׀ מָ֘הִ֤יר בִּמְלַאכְתּ֗וֹ לִֽפְנֵֽי־מְלָכִ֥ים יִתְיַצָּ֑ב בַּל־יִ֝תְיַצֵּב לִפְנֵ֥י חֲשֻׁכִּֽים׃

lines.text: Do you see a man skilled in his work? He will serve kings. He won’t serve obscure men.
Hast thou seen a man speedy in his business? Before kings he doth station himself, He stations not himself before obscure men!

23.he: כִּֽי־תֵ֭שֵׁב לִלְח֣וֹם אֶת־מוֹשֵׁ֑ל בִּ֥ין תָּ֝בִ֗ין אֶת־אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְפָנֶֽיךָ׃

lines.text: When you sit to eat with a ruler, consider diligently what is before you;
When thou sittest to eat with a ruler, Thou considerest diligently that which [is] before thee,

23.he: וְשַׂמְתָּ֣ שַׂכִּ֣ין בְּלֹעֶ֑ךָ אִם־בַּ֖עַל נֶ֣פֶשׁ אָֽתָּה׃

lines.text: put a knife to your throat, if you are a man given to appetite.
And thou hast put a knife to thy throat, If thou [art] a man of appetite.

23.he: אַל־תִּ֭תְאָו לְמַטְעַמּוֹתָ֑יו וְ֝ה֗וּא לֶ֣חֶם כְּזָבִֽים׃

lines.text: Don’t be desirous of his dainties, since they are deceitful food.
Have no desire to his dainties, seeing it [is] lying food.

23.he: אַל־תִּיגַ֥ע לְֽהַעֲשִׁ֑יר מִֽבִּינָתְךָ֥ חֲדָֽל׃

lines.text: Don’t weary yourself to be rich. In your wisdom, show restraint.
Labour not to make wealth, From thine own understanding cease, Dost thou cause thine eyes to fly upon it? Then it is not.

23.he: התעוף עֵינֶ֥יךָ בּ֗וֹ וְֽאֵ֫ינֶ֥נּוּ כִּ֤י עָשֹׂ֣ה יַעֲשֶׂה־לּ֣וֹ כְנָפַ֑יִם כְּ֝נֶ֗שֶׁר ועיף הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

lines.text: Why do you set your eyes on that which is not? For it certainly sprouts wings like an eagle and flies in the sky.
For wealth maketh to itself wings, As an eagle it flieth to the heavens.

23.he: אַל־תִּלְחַ֗ם אֶת־לֶ֭חֶם רַ֣ע עָ֑יִן וְאַל־תתאו לְמַטְעַמֹּתָֽיו׃

lines.text: Don’t eat the food of him who has a stingy eye, and don’t crave his delicacies:
Eat not the bread of an evil eye, And have no desire to his dainties,

23.he: כִּ֤י ׀ כְּמוֹ־שָׁעַ֥ר בְּנַפְשׁ֗וֹ כֶּ֫ן־ה֥וּא אֱכֹ֣ל וּ֭שְׁתֵה יֹ֣אמַר לָ֑ךְ וְ֝לִבּ֗וֹ בַּל־עִמָּֽךְ׃

lines.text: for as he thinks about the cost, so he is. “Eat and drink!” he says to you, but his heart is not with you.
For as he hath thought in his soul, so [is] he, 'Eat and drink,' saith he to thee, And his heart [is] not with thee.

23.he: פִּֽתְּךָ־אָכַ֥לְתָּ תְקִיאֶ֑נָּה וְ֝שִׁחַ֗תָּ דְּבָרֶ֥יךָ הַנְּעִימִֽים׃

lines.text: The morsel which you have eaten you shall vomit up, and lose your good words.
Thy morsel thou hast eaten thou dost vomit up, And hast marred thy words that [are] sweet.

23.he: בְּאָזְנֵ֣י כְ֭סִיל אַל־תְּדַבֵּ֑ר כִּֽי־יָ֝ב֗וּז לְשֵׂ֣כֶל מִלֶּֽיךָ׃

lines.text: Don’t speak in the ears of a fool, for he will despise the wisdom of your words.
In the ears of a fool speak not, For he treadeth on the wisdom of thy words.

23.he: אַל־תַּ֭סֵּג גְּב֣וּל עוֹלָ֑ם וּבִשְׂדֵ֥י יְ֝תוֹמִ֗ים אַל־תָּבֹֽא׃

lines.text: Don’t move the ancient boundary stone. Don’t encroach on the fields of the fatherless,
Remove not a border of olden times, And into fields of the fatherless enter not,

23.he: כִּֽי־גֹאֲלָ֥ם חָזָ֑ק הֽוּא־יָרִ֖יב אֶת־רִיבָ֣ם אִתָּֽךְ׃

lines.text: for their Defender is strong. He will plead their case against you.
For their Redeemer [is] strong, He doth plead their cause with thee.

23.he: הָבִ֣יאָה לַמּוּסָ֣ר לִבֶּ֑ךָ וְ֝אָזְנֶ֗ךָ לְאִמְרֵי־דָֽעַת׃

lines.text: Apply your heart to instruction, and your ears to the words of knowledge.
Bring in to instruction thy heart, And thine ear to sayings of knowledge.

23.he: אַל־תִּמְנַ֣ע מִנַּ֣עַר מוּסָ֑ר כִּֽי־תַכֶּ֥נּוּ בַ֝שֵּׁ֗בֶט לֹ֣א יָמֽוּת׃

lines.text: Don’t withhold correction from a child. If you punish him with the rod, he will not die.
Withhold not from a youth chastisement, When thou smitest him with a rod he dieth not.

23.he: אַ֭תָּה בַּשֵּׁ֣בֶט תַּכֶּ֑נּוּ וְ֝נַפְשׁ֗וֹ מִשְּׁא֥וֹל תַּצִּֽיל׃

lines.text: Punish him with the rod, and save his soul from Sheol.
Thou with a rod smitest him, And his soul from Sheol thou deliverest.

23.he: בְּ֭נִי אִם־חָכַ֣ם לִבֶּ֑ךָ יִשְׂמַ֖ח לִבִּ֣י גַם־אָֽנִי׃

lines.text: My son, if your heart is wise, then my heart will be glad, even mine.
My son, if thy heart hath been wise, My heart rejoiceth, even mine,

23.he: וְתַעְלֹ֥זְנָה כִלְיוֹתָ֑י בְּדַבֵּ֥ר שְׂ֝פָתֶ֗יךָ מֵישָׁרִֽים׃

lines.text: Yes, my heart will rejoice when your lips speak what is right.
And my reins exult when thy lips speak uprightly.

23.he: אַל־יְקַנֵּ֣א לִ֭בְּךָ בַּֽחַטָּאִ֑ים כִּ֥י אִם־בְּיִרְאַת־יְ֝הוָ֗ה כָּל־הַיּֽוֹם׃

lines.text: Don’t let your heart envy sinners, but rather fear Yahweh all day long.
Let not thy heart be envious at sinners, But — in the fear of Jehovah all the day.

23.he: כִּ֭י אִם־יֵ֣שׁ אַחֲרִ֑ית וְ֝תִקְוָתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א תִכָּרֵֽת׃

lines.text: Indeed surely there is a future hope, and your hope will not be cut off.
For, is there a posterity? Then thy hope is not cut off.

23.he: שְׁמַע־אַתָּ֣ה בְנִ֣י וַחֲכָ֑ם וְאַשֵּׁ֖ר בַּדֶּ֣רֶךְ לִבֶּֽךָ׃

lines.text: Listen, my son, and be wise, and keep your heart on the right path!
Hear thou, my son, and be wise, And make happy in the way thy heart,

23.he: אַל־תְּהִ֥י בְסֹֽבְאֵי־יָ֑יִן בְּזֹלֲלֵ֖י בָשָׂ֣ר לָֽמוֹ׃

lines.text: Don’t be among ones drinking too much wine, or those who gorge themselves on meat:
Be not thou among quaffers of wine, Among gluttonous ones of flesh,

23.he: כִּי־סֹבֵ֣א וְ֭זוֹלֵל יִוָּרֵ֑שׁ וּ֝קְרָעִ֗ים תַּלְבִּ֥ישׁ נוּמָֽה׃

lines.text: for the drunkard and the glutton shall become poor; and drowsiness clothes them in rags.
For the quaffer and glutton become poor, And drowsiness clotheth with rags.

23.he: שְׁמַ֣ע לְ֭אָבִיךָ זֶ֣ה יְלָדֶ֑ךָ וְאַל־תָּ֝ב֗וּז כִּֽי־זָקְנָ֥ה אִמֶּֽךָ׃

lines.text: Listen to your father who gave you life, and don’t despise your mother when she is old.
Hearken to thy father, who begat thee, And despise not thy mother when she hath become old.

23.he: אֱמֶ֣ת קְ֭נֵה וְאַל־תִּמְכֹּ֑ר חָכְמָ֖ה וּמוּסָ֣ר וּבִינָֽה׃

lines.text: Buy the truth, and don’t sell it. Get wisdom, discipline, and understanding.
Truth buy, and sell not, Wisdom, and instruction, and understanding,

23.he: גול יגול אֲבִ֣י צַדִּ֑יק יולד חָ֝כָ֗ם וישמח־בּֽוֹ׃

lines.text: The father of the righteous has great joy. Whoever fathers a wise child delights in him.
The father of the righteous rejoiceth greatly, The begetter of the wise rejoiceth in him.

23.he: יִֽשְׂמַח־אָבִ֥יךָ וְאִמֶּ֑ךָ וְ֝תָגֵ֗ל יֽוֹלַדְתֶּֽךָ׃

lines.text: Let your father and your mother be glad! Let her who bore you rejoice!
Rejoice doth thy father and thy mother, Yea, she that bare thee is joyful.

23.he: תְּנָֽה־בְנִ֣י לִבְּךָ֣ לִ֑י וְ֝עֵינֶ֗יךָ דְּרָכַ֥י תרצנה׃

lines.text: My son, give me your heart; and let your eyes keep in my ways.
Give, my son, thy heart to me, And let thine eyes watch my ways.

23.he: כִּֽי־שׁוּחָ֣ה עֲמֻקָּ֣ה זוֹנָ֑ה וּבְאֵ֥ר צָ֝רָ֗ה נָכְרִיָּֽה׃

lines.text: For a prostitute is a deep pit; and a wayward wife is a narrow well.
For a harlot [is] a deep ditch, And a strange woman [is] a strait pit.

23.he: אַף־הִ֭יא כְּחֶ֣תֶף תֶּֽאֱרֹ֑ב וּ֝בוֹגְדִ֗ים בְּאָדָ֥ם תּוֹסִֽף׃

lines.text: Yes, she lies in wait like a robber, and increases the unfaithful among men.
She also, as catching prey, lieth in wait, And the treacherous among men she increaseth.

23.he: לְמִ֨י א֥וֹי לְמִ֪י אֲב֡וֹי לְמִ֤י מדונים ׀ לְמִ֥י שִׂ֗יחַ לְ֭מִי פְּצָעִ֣ים חִנָּ֑ם לְ֝מִ֗י חַכְלִל֥וּת עֵינָֽיִם׃

lines.text: Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has strife? Who has complaints? Who has needless bruises? Who has bloodshot eyes?
Who hath woe? who hath sorrow? Who hath contentions? who hath plaint? Who hath wounds without cause? Who hath redness of eyes?

23.he: לַֽמְאַחֲרִ֥ים עַל־הַיָּ֑יִן לַ֝בָּאִ֗ים לַחְקֹ֥ר מִמְסָֽךְ׃

lines.text: Those who stay long at the wine; those who go to seek out mixed wine.
Those tarrying by the wine, Those going in to search out mixed wine.

23.he: אַל־תֵּ֥רֶא יַּיִן֮ כִּ֪י יִתְאַ֫דָּ֥ם כִּֽי־יִתֵּ֣ן בכיס עֵינ֑וֹ יִ֝תְהַלֵּ֗ךְ בְּמֵישָׁרִֽים׃

lines.text: Don’t look at the wine when it is red, when it sparkles in the cup, when it goes down smoothly.
See not wine when it showeth itself red, When it giveth in the cup its colour, It goeth up and down through the upright.

23.he: אַ֭חֲרִיתוֹ כְּנָחָ֣שׁ יִשָּׁ֑ךְ וּֽכְצִפְעֹנִ֥י יַפְרִֽשׁ׃

lines.text: In the end, it bites like a snake, and poisons like a viper.
Its latter end — as a serpent it biteth, And as a basilisk it stingeth.

23.he: עֵ֭ינֶיךָ יִרְא֣וּ זָר֑וֹת וְ֝לִבְּךָ֗ יְדַבֵּ֥ר תַּהְפֻּכֽוֹת׃

lines.text: Your eyes will see strange things, and your mind will imagine confusing things.
Thine eyes see strange women, And thy heart speaketh perverse things.

23.he: וְ֭הָיִיתָ כְּשֹׁכֵ֣ב בְּלֶב־יָ֑ם וּ֝כְשֹׁכֵ֗ב בְּרֹ֣אשׁ חִבֵּֽל׃

lines.text: Yes, you will be as he who lies down in the middle of the sea, or as he who lies on top of the rigging:
And thou hast been as one lying down in the heart of the sea, And as one lying down on the top of a mast.

23.he: הִכּ֥וּנִי בַל־חָלִיתִי֮ הֲלָמ֗וּנִי בַּל־יָ֫דָ֥עְתִּי מָתַ֥י אָקִ֑יץ א֝וֹסִ֗יף אֲבַקְשֶׁ֥נּוּ עֽוֹד׃

lines.text: “They hit me, and I was not hurt! They beat me, and I don’t feel it! When will I wake up? I can do it again. I can find another.”
'They smote me, I have not been sick, They beat me, I have not known. When I awake — I seek it yet again!'

24.he: אַל־תְּ֭קַנֵּא בְּאַנְשֵׁ֣י רָעָ֑ה וְאַל־תתאו לִהְי֥וֹת אִתָּֽם׃

lines.text: Don’t be envious of evil men, neither desire to be with them;
Be not envious of evil men, And desire not to be with them.

24.he: כִּי־שֹׁ֭ד יֶהְגֶּ֣ה לִבָּ֑ם וְ֝עָמָ֗ל שִׂפְתֵיהֶ֥ם תְּדַבֵּֽרְנָה׃

lines.text: for their hearts plot violence and their lips talk about mischief.
For destruction doth their heart meditate, And perverseness do their lips speak.

24.he: בְּ֭חָכְמָה יִבָּ֣נֶה בָּ֑יִת וּ֝בִתְבוּנָ֗ה יִתְכּוֹנָֽן׃

lines.text: Through wisdom a house is built; by understanding it is established;
By wisdom is a house builded, And by understanding it establisheth itself.

24.he: וּ֭בְדַעַת חֲדָרִ֣ים יִמָּלְא֑וּ כָּל־ה֖וֹן יָקָ֣ר וְנָעִֽים׃

lines.text: by knowledge the rooms are filled with all rare and beautiful treasure.
And by knowledge the inner parts are filled, [With] all precious and pleasant wealth.

24.he: גֶּֽבֶר־חָכָ֥ם בַּע֑וֹז וְאִֽישׁ־דַּ֝֗עַת מְאַמֶּץ־כֹּֽחַ׃

lines.text: A wise man has great power; and a knowledgeable man increases strength;
Mighty [is] the wise in strength, And a man of knowledge is strengthening power,

24.he: כִּ֣י בְ֭תַחְבֻּלוֹת תַּעֲשֶׂה־לְּךָ֣ מִלְחָמָ֑ה וּ֝תְשׁוּעָ֗ה בְּרֹ֣ב יוֹעֵֽץ׃

lines.text: for by wise guidance you wage your war; and victory is in many advisors.
For by plans thou makest for thyself war, And deliverance [is] in a multitude of counsellors.

24.he: רָאמ֣וֹת לֶֽאֱוִ֣יל חָכְמ֑וֹת בַּ֝שַּׁ֗עַר לֹ֣א יִפְתַּח־פִּֽיהוּ׃

lines.text: Wisdom is too high for a fool. He doesn’t open his mouth in the gate.
Wisdom [is] high for a fool, In the gate he openeth not his mouth.

24.he: מְחַשֵּׁ֥ב לְהָרֵ֑עַ ל֝֗וֹ בַּֽעַל־מְזִמּ֥וֹת יִקְרָֽאוּ׃

lines.text: One who plots to do evil will be called a schemer.
Whoso is devising to do evil, Him they call a master of wicked thoughts.

24.he: זִמַּ֣ת אִוֶּ֣לֶת חַטָּ֑את וְתוֹעֲבַ֖ת לְאָדָ֣ם לֵֽץ׃

lines.text: The schemes of folly are sin. The mocker is detested by men.
The thought of folly [is] sin, And an abomination to man [is] a scorner.

24.he: הִ֭תְרַפִּיתָ בְּי֥וֹם צָרָ֗ה צַ֣ר כֹּחֶֽכָה׃

lines.text: If you falter in the time of trouble, your strength is small.
Thou hast shewed thyself weak in a day of adversity, Straitened is thy power,

24.he: הַ֭צֵּל לְקֻחִ֣ים לַמָּ֑וֶת וּמָטִ֥ים לַ֝הֶ֗רֶג אִם־תַּחְשֽׂוֹךְ׃

lines.text: Rescue those who are being led away to death! Indeed, hold back those who are staggering to the slaughter!
If [from] delivering those taken to death, And those slipping to the slaughter — thou keepest back.

24.he: כִּֽי־תֹאמַ֗ר הֵן֮ לֹא־יָדַ֪עְנ֫וּ זֶ֥ה הֲֽלֹא־תֹ֘כֵ֤ן לִבּ֨וֹת ׀ הֽוּא־יָבִ֗ין וְנֹצֵ֣ר נַ֭פְשְׁךָ ה֣וּא יֵדָ֑ע וְהֵשִׁ֖יב לְאָדָ֣ם כְּפָעֳלֽוֹ׃

lines.text: If you say, “Behold, we didn’t know this,” doesn’t he who weighs the hearts consider it? He who keeps your soul, doesn’t he know it? Shall he not render to every man according to his work?
When thou sayest, 'Lo, we knew not this.' Is not the Ponderer of hearts He who understandeth? And the Keeper of thy soul He who knoweth? And He hath rendered to man according to his work.

24.he: אֱכָל־בְּנִ֣י דְבַ֣שׁ כִּי־ט֑וֹב וְנֹ֥פֶת מָ֝ת֗וֹק עַל־חִכֶּֽךָ׃

lines.text: My son, eat honey, for it is good, the droppings of the honeycomb, which are sweet to your taste;
Eat my son, honey that [is] good, And the honeycomb — sweet to thy palate.

24.he: כֵּ֤ן ׀ דְּעֶ֥ה חָכְמָ֗ה לְנַ֫פְשֶׁ֥ךָ אִם־מָ֭צָאתָ וְיֵ֣שׁ אַחֲרִ֑ית וְ֝תִקְוָתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א תִכָּרֵֽת׃

lines.text: so you shall know wisdom to be to your soul. If you have found it, then there will be a reward: Your hope will not be cut off.
So [is] the knowledge of wisdom to thy soul, If thou hast found that there is a posterity And thy hope is not cut off.

24.he: אַל־תֶּאֱרֹ֣ב רָ֭שָׁע לִנְוֵ֣ה צַדִּ֑יק אַֽל־תְּשַׁדֵּ֥ד רִבְצוֹ׃

lines.text: Don’t lay in wait, wicked man, against the habitation of the righteous. Don’t destroy his resting place;
Lay not wait, O wicked one, At the habitation of the righteous. Do not spoil his resting-place.

24.he: כִּ֤י שֶׁ֨בַע ׀ יִפּ֣וֹל צַדִּ֣יק וָקָ֑ם וּ֝רְשָׁעִ֗ים יִכָּשְׁל֥וּ בְרָעָֽה׃

lines.text: for a righteous man falls seven times and rises up again; but the wicked are overthrown by calamity.
For seven [times] doth the righteous fall and rise, And the wicked stumble in evil.

24.he: בִּנְפֹ֣ל אויביך אַל־תִּשְׂמָ֑ח וּ֝בִכָּשְׁל֗וֹ אַל־יָגֵ֥ל לִבֶּֽךָ׃

lines.text: Don’t rejoice when your enemy falls. Don’t let your heart be glad when he is overthrown,
In the falling of thine enemy rejoice not, And in his stumbling let not thy heart be joyful,

24.he: פֶּן־יִרְאֶ֣ה יְ֭הוָה וְרַ֣ע בְּעֵינָ֑יו וְהֵשִׁ֖יב מֵעָלָ֣יו אַפּֽוֹ׃

lines.text: lest Yahweh see it, and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him.
Lest Jehovah see, and [it be] evil in His eyes, And He hath turned from off him His anger.

24.he: אַל־תִּתְחַ֥ר בַּמְּרֵעִ֑ים אַל־תְּ֝קַנֵּ֗א בָּרְשָׁעִֽים׃

lines.text: Don’t fret yourself because of evildoers, neither be envious of the wicked;
Fret not thyself at evil doers, Be not envious at the wicked,

24.he: כִּ֤י ׀ לֹֽא־תִהְיֶ֣ה אַחֲרִ֣ית לָרָ֑ע נֵ֖ר רְשָׁעִ֣ים יִדְעָֽךְ׃

lines.text: for there will be no reward to the evil man. The lamp of the wicked will be snuffed out.
For there is not a posterity to the evil, The lamp of the wicked is extinguished.

24.he: יְרָֽא־אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה בְּנִ֣י וָמֶ֑לֶךְ עִם־שׁ֝וֹנִ֗ים אַל־תִּתְעָרָֽב׃

lines.text: My son, fear Yahweh and the king. Don’t join those who are rebellious;
Fear Jehovah, my son, and the king, With changers mix not up thyself,

24.he: כִּֽי־פִ֭תְאֹם יָק֣וּם אֵידָ֑ם וּפִ֥יד שְׁ֝נֵיהֶ֗ם מִ֣י יוֹדֵֽעַ׃

lines.text: for their calamity will rise suddenly. Who knows what destruction may come from them both?
For suddenly doth their calamity rise, And the ruin of them both — who knoweth!

24.he: גַּם־אֵ֥לֶּה לַֽחֲכָמִ֑ים הַֽכֵּר־פָּנִ֖ים בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט בַּל־טֽוֹב׃

lines.text: These also are sayings of the wise. To show partiality in judgment is not good.
These also are for the wise: — To discern faces in judgment is not good.

24.he: אֹ֤מֵ֨ר ׀ לְרָשָׁע֮ צַדִּ֪יק אָ֥תָּה יִקְּבֻ֥הוּ עַמִּ֑ים יִזְעָמ֥וּהוּ לְאֻמִּֽים׃

lines.text: He who says to the wicked, “You are righteous,” peoples will curse him, and nations will abhor him—
Whoso is saying to the wicked, 'Thou [art] righteous,' Peoples execrate him — nations abhor him.

24.he: וְלַמּוֹכִיחִ֥ים יִנְעָ֑ם וַֽ֝עֲלֵיהֶ֗ם תָּב֥וֹא בִרְכַּת־טֹֽוּב׃

lines.text: but it will go well with those who convict the guilty, and a rich blessing will come on them.
And to those reproving it is pleasant, And on them cometh a good blessing.

24.he: שְׂפָתַ֥יִם יִשָּׁ֑ק מֵ֝שִׁ֗יב דְּבָרִ֥ים נְכֹחִֽים׃

lines.text: An honest answer is like a kiss on the lips.
Lips he kisseth who is returning straightforward words.

24.he: הָ֘כֵ֤ן בַּח֨וּץ ׀ מְלַאכְתֶּ֗ךָ וְעַתְּדָ֣הּ בַּשָּׂדֶ֣ה לָ֑ךְ אַ֝חַ֗ר וּבָנִ֥יתָ בֵיתֶֽךָ׃

lines.text: Prepare your work outside, and get your fields ready. Afterwards, build your house.
Prepare in an out-place thy work, And make it ready in the field — go afterwards, Then thou hast built thy house.

24.he: אַל־תְּהִ֣י עֵד־חִנָּ֣ם בְּרֵעֶ֑ךָ וַ֝הֲפִתִּ֗יתָ בִּשְׂפָתֶֽיךָ׃

lines.text: Don’t be a witness against your neighbor without cause. Don’t deceive with your lips.
Be not a witness for nought against thy neighbour, Or thou hast enticed with thy lips.

24.he: אַל־תֹּאמַ֗ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָֽשָׂה־לִ֭י כֵּ֤ן אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־לּ֑וֹ אָשִׁ֖יב לָאִ֣ישׁ כְּפָעֳלֽוֹ׃

lines.text: Don’t say, “I will do to him as he has done to me; I will repay the man according to his work.”
Say not, 'As he did to me, so I do to him, I render to each according to his work.'

24.he: עַל־שְׂדֵ֣ה אִישׁ־עָצֵ֣ל עָבַ֑רְתִּי וְעַל־כֶּ֝֗רֶם אָדָ֥ם חֲסַר־לֵֽב׃

lines.text: I went by the field of the sluggard, by the vineyard of the man void of understanding:
Near the field of a slothful man I passed by, And near the vineyard of a man lacking heart.

24.he: וְהִנֵּ֨ה עָ֘לָ֤ה כֻלּ֨וֹ ׀ קִמְּשֹׂנִ֗ים כָּסּ֣וּ פָנָ֣יו חֲרֻלִּ֑ים וְגֶ֖דֶר אֲבָנָ֣יו נֶהֱרָֽסָה׃

lines.text: Behold, it was all grown over with thorns. Its surface was covered with nettles, and its stone wall was broken down.
And lo, it hath gone up — all of it — thorns! Covered its face have nettles, And its stone wall hath been broken down.

24.he: וָֽאֶחֱזֶ֣ה אָ֭נֹכִֽי אָשִׁ֣ית לִבִּ֑י רָ֝אִ֗יתִי לָקַ֥חְתִּי מוּסָּֽר׃

lines.text: Then I saw, and considered well. I saw, and received instruction:
And I see — I — I do set my heart, I have seen — I have received instruction,

24.he: מְעַ֣ט שֵׁ֭נוֹת מְעַ֣ט תְּנוּמ֑וֹת מְעַ֓ט ׀ חִבֻּ֖ק יָדַ֣יִם לִשְׁכָּֽב׃

lines.text: a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep,
A little sleep — a little slumber — A little folding of the hands to lie down.

24.he: וּבָֽא־מִתְהַלֵּ֥ךְ רֵישֶׁ֑ךָ וּ֝מַחְסֹרֶ֗יךָ כְּאִ֣ישׁ מָגֵֽן׃

lines.text: so your poverty will come as a robber and your want as an armed man.
And thy poverty hath come [as] a traveller, And thy want as an armed man!

25.he: גַּם־אֵ֭לֶּה מִשְׁלֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶ֝עְתִּ֗יקוּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י ׀ חִזְקִיָּ֬ה מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָֽה׃

lines.text: These also are proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.
Also these are Proverbs of Solomon, that men of Hezekiah king of Judah transcribed: —

25.he: כְּבֹ֣ד אֱ֭לֹהִים הַסְתֵּ֣ר דָּבָ֑ר וּכְבֹ֥ד מְ֝לָכִ֗ים חֲקֹ֣ר דָּבָֽר׃

lines.text: It is the glory of God to conceal a thing, but the glory of kings is to search out a matter.
The honour of God [is] to hide a thing, And the honour of kings to search out a matter.

25.he: שָׁמַ֣יִם לָ֭רוּם וָאָ֣רֶץ לָעֹ֑מֶק וְלֵ֥ב מְ֝לָכִ֗ים אֵ֣ין חֵֽקֶר׃

lines.text: As the heavens for height, and the earth for depth, so the hearts of kings are unsearchable.
The heavens for height, and the earth for depth, And the heart of kings — [are] unsearchable.

25.he: הָג֣וֹ סִיגִ֣ים מִכָּ֑סֶף וַיֵּצֵ֖א לַצֹּרֵ֣ף כֶּֽלִי׃

lines.text: Take away the dross from the silver, and material comes out for the refiner;
Take away dross from silver, And a vessel for the refiner goeth forth,

25.he: הָג֣וֹ רָ֭שָׁע לִפְנֵי־מֶ֑לֶךְ וְיִכּ֖וֹן בַּצֶּ֣דֶק כִּסְאֽוֹ׃

lines.text: Take away the wicked from the king’s presence, and his throne will be established in righteousness.
Take away the wicked before a king, And established in righteousness is his throne.

25.he: אַל־תִּתְהַדַּ֥ר לִפְנֵי־מֶ֑לֶךְ וּבִמְק֥וֹם גְּ֝דֹלִ֗ים אַֽל־תַּעֲמֹֽד׃

lines.text: Don’t exalt yourself in the presence of the king, or claim a place among great men;
Honour not thyself before a king, And in the place of the great stand not.

25.he: כִּ֤י ט֥וֹב אֲמָר־לְךָ֗ עֲֽלֵ֫ה הֵ֥נָּה מֵֽ֭הַשְׁפִּ֣ילְךָ לִפְנֵ֣י נָדִ֑יב אֲשֶׁ֖ר רָא֣וּ עֵינֶֽיךָ׃

lines.text: for it is better that it be said to you, “Come up here,” than that you should be put lower in the presence of the prince, whom your eyes have seen.
For better [that] he hath said to thee, 'Come thou up hither,' Than [that] he humble thee before a noble, Whom thine eyes have seen.

25.he: אַל־תֵּצֵ֥א לָרִ֗ב מַ֫הֵ֥ר פֶּ֣ן מַה־תַּ֭עֲשֶׂה בְּאַחֲרִיתָ֑הּ בְּהַכְלִ֖ים אֹתְךָ֣ רֵעֶֽךָ׃

lines.text: Don’t be hasty in bringing charges to court. What will you do in the end when your neighbor shames you?
Go not forth to strive, haste, turn, What dost thou in its latter end, When thy neighbour causeth thee to blush?

25.he: רִֽ֭יבְךָ רִ֣יב אֶת־רֵעֶ֑ךָ וְס֖וֹד אַחֵ֣ר אַל־תְּגָֽל׃

lines.text: Debate your case with your neighbor, and don’t betray the confidence of another,
Thy cause plead with thy neighbour, And the secret counsel of another reveal not,

25.he: פֶּֽן־יְחַסֶּדְךָ֥ שֹׁמֵ֑עַ וְ֝דִבָּתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א תָשֽׁוּב׃

lines.text: lest one who hears it put you to shame, and your bad reputation never depart.
Lest the hearer put thee to shame, And thine evil report turn not back.

25.he: תַּפּוּחֵ֣י זָ֭הָב בְּמַשְׂכִּיּ֣וֹת כָּ֑סֶף דָּ֝בָ֗ר דָּבֻ֥ר עַל־אָפְנָֽיו׃

lines.text: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.
Apples of gold in imagery of silver, [Is] the word spoken at its fit times.

25.he: נֶ֣זֶם זָ֭הָב וַחֲלִי־כָ֑תֶם מוֹכִ֥יחַ חָ֝כָ֗ם עַל־אֹ֥זֶן שֹׁמָֽעַת׃

lines.text: As an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, so is a wise reprover to an obedient ear.
A ring of gold, and an ornament of pure gold, [Is] the wise reprover to an attentive ear.

25.he: כְּצִנַּת־שֶׁ֨לֶג ׀ בְּי֬וֹם קָצִ֗יר צִ֣יר נֶ֭אֱמָן לְשֹׁלְחָ֑יו וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ אֲדֹנָ֣יו יָשִֽׁיב׃

lines.text: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, so is a faithful messenger to those who send him; for he refreshes the soul of his masters.
As a vessel of snow in a day of harvest, [So is] a faithful ambassador to those sending him, And the soul of his masters he refresheth.

25.he: נְשִׂיאִ֣ים וְ֭רוּחַ וְגֶ֣שֶׁם אָ֑יִן אִ֥ישׁ מִ֝תְהַלֵּ֗ל בְּמַתַּת־שָֽׁקֶר׃

lines.text: As clouds and wind without rain, so is he who boasts of gifts deceptively.
Clouds and wind, and rain there is none, [Is] a man boasting himself in a false gift.

25.he: בְּאֹ֣רֶךְ אַ֭פַּיִם יְפֻתֶּ֣ה קָצִ֑ין וְלָשׁ֥וֹן רַ֝כָּ֗ה תִּשְׁבָּר־גָּֽרֶם׃

lines.text: By patience a ruler is persuaded. A soft tongue breaks the bone.
By long-suffering is a ruler persuaded, And a soft tongue breaketh a bone.

25.he: דְּבַ֣שׁ מָ֭צָאתָ אֱכֹ֣ל דַּיֶּ֑ךָּ פֶּן־תִּ֝שְׂבָּעֶ֗נּוּ וַהֲקֵֽאתֽוֹ׃

lines.text: Have you found honey? Eat as much as is sufficient for you, lest you eat too much, and vomit it.
Honey thou hast found — eat thy sufficiency, Lest thou be satiated [with] it, and hast vomited it.

25.he: הֹקַ֣ר רַ֭גְלְךָ מִבֵּ֣ית רֵעֶ֑ךָ פֶּן־יִ֝שְׂבָּעֲךָ֗ וּשְׂנֵאֶֽךָ׃

lines.text: Let your foot be seldom in your neighbor’s house, lest he be weary of you, and hate you.
Withdraw thy foot from thy neighbour's house, Lest he be satiated [with] thee, and have hated thee.

25.he: מֵפִ֣יץ וְ֭חֶרֶב וְחֵ֣ץ שָׁנ֑וּן אִ֥ישׁ עֹנֶ֥ה בְ֝רֵעֵ֗הוּ עֵ֣ד שָֽׁקֶר׃

lines.text: A man who gives false testimony against his neighbor is like a club, a sword, or a sharp arrow.
A maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow, [Is] the man testifying against his neighbour a false testimony.

25.he: שֵׁ֣ן רֹ֭עָה וְרֶ֣גֶל מוּעָ֑דֶת מִבְטָ֥ח בּ֝וֹגֵ֗ד בְּי֣וֹם צָרָֽה׃

lines.text: Confidence in someone unfaithful in time of trouble is like a bad tooth or a lame foot.
A bad tooth, and a tottering foot, [Is] the confidence of the treacherous in a day of adversity.

25.he: מַ֥עֲדֶה בֶּ֨גֶד ׀ בְּי֣וֹם קָ֭רָה חֹ֣מֶץ עַל־נָ֑תֶר וְשָׁ֥ר בַּ֝שִּׁרִ֗ים עַ֣ל לֶב־רָֽע׃

lines.text: As one who takes away a garment in cold weather, or vinegar on soda, so is one who sings songs to a heavy heart.
Whoso is taking away a garment in a cold day, [Is as] vinegar on nitre, And a singer of songs on a sad heart.

25.he: אִם־רָעֵ֣ב שֹׂ֭נַאֲךָ הַאֲכִלֵ֣הוּ לָ֑חֶם וְאִם־צָ֝מֵ֗א הַשְׁקֵ֥הוּ מָֽיִם׃

lines.text: If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat. If he is thirsty, give him water to drink;
If he who is hating thee doth hunger, cause him to eat bread, And if he thirst, cause him to drink water.

25.he: כִּ֤י גֶֽחָלִ֗ים אַ֭תָּה חֹתֶ֣ה עַל־רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וַֽ֝יהוָ֗ה יְשַׁלֶּם־לָֽךְ׃

lines.text: for you will heap coals of fire on his head, and Yahweh will reward you.
For coals thou art putting on his head, And Jehovah giveth recompense to thee.

25.he: ר֣וּחַ צָ֭פוֹן תְּח֣וֹלֵֽל גָּ֑שֶׁם וּפָנִ֥ים נִ֝זְעָמִ֗ים לְשׁ֣וֹן סָֽתֶר׃

lines.text: The north wind produces rain; so a backbiting tongue brings an angry face.
A north wind bringeth forth rain, And a secret tongue — indignant faces.

25.he: ט֗וֹב שֶׁ֥בֶת עַל־פִּנַּת־גָּ֑ג מֵאֵ֥שֶׁת מדונים וּבֵ֥ית חָֽבֶר׃

lines.text: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop than to share a house with a contentious woman.
Better to sit on a corner of a roof, Than [with] a woman of contentions, and a house of company.

25.he: מַ֣יִם קָ֭רִים עַל־נֶ֣פֶשׁ עֲיֵפָ֑ה וּשְׁמוּעָ֥ה ט֝וֹבָ֗ה מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מֶרְחָֽק׃

lines.text: Like cold water to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a far country.
[As] cold waters for a weary soul, So [is] a good report from a far country.

25.he: מַעְיָ֣ן נִ֭רְפָּשׂ וּמָק֣וֹר מָשְׁחָ֑ת צַ֝דִּ֗יק מָ֣ט לִפְנֵֽי־רָשָֽׁע׃

lines.text: Like a muddied spring and a polluted well, so is a righteous man who gives way before the wicked.
A spring troubled, and a fountain corrupt, [Is] the righteous falling before the wicked.

25.he: אָ֘כֹ֤ל דְּבַ֣שׁ הַרְבּ֣וֹת לֹּא־ט֑וֹב וְחֵ֖קֶר כְּבֹדָ֣ם כָּבֽוֹד׃

lines.text: It is not good to eat much honey, nor is it honorable to seek one’s own honor.
The eating of much honey is not good, Nor a searching out of one's own honour — honour.

25.he: עִ֣יר פְּ֭רוּצָה אֵ֣ין חוֹמָ֑ה אִ֝֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֵ֖ין מַעְצָ֣ר לְרוּחֽוֹ׃

lines.text: Like a city that is broken down and without walls is a man whose spirit is without restraint.
A city broken down without walls, [Is] a man without restraint over his spirit!

26.he: כַּשֶּׁ֤לֶג ׀ בַּקַּ֗יִץ וְכַמָּטָ֥ר בַּקָּצִ֑יר כֵּ֤ן לֹא־נָאוֶ֖ה לִכְסִ֣יל כָּבֽוֹד׃

lines.text: Like snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honor is not fitting for a fool.
As snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, So honour [is] not comely for a fool.

26.he: כַּצִּפּ֣וֹר לָ֭נוּד כַּדְּר֣וֹר לָע֑וּף כֵּ֥ן קִֽלְלַ֥ת חִ֝נָּ֗ם לא תָבֹֽא׃

lines.text: Like a fluttering sparrow, like a darting swallow, so the undeserved curse doesn’t come to rest.
As a bird by wandering, as a swallow by flying, So reviling without cause doth not come.

26.he: שׁ֣וֹט לַ֭סּוּס מֶ֣תֶג לַחֲמ֑וֹר וְ֝שֵׁ֗בֶט לְגֵ֣ו כְּסִילִֽים׃

lines.text: A whip is for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the back of fools!
A whip is for a horse, a bridle for an ass, And a rod for the back of fools.

26.he: אַל־תַּ֣עַן כְּ֭סִיל כְּאִוַּלְתּ֑וֹ פֶּֽן־תִּשְׁוֶה־לּ֥וֹ גַם־אָֽתָּה׃

lines.text: Don’t answer a fool according to his folly, lest you also be like him.
Answer not a fool according to his folly, Lest thou be like to him — even thou.

26.he: עֲנֵ֣ה כְ֭סִיל כְּאִוַּלְתּ֑וֹ פֶּן־יִהְיֶ֖ה חָכָ֣ם בְּעֵינָֽיו׃

lines.text: Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own eyes.
Answer a fool according to his folly, Lest he be wise in his own eyes.

26.he: מְקַצֶּ֣ה רַ֭גְלַיִם חָמָ֣ס שֹׁתֶ֑ה שֹׁלֵ֖חַ דְּבָרִ֣ים בְּיַד־כְּסִֽיל׃

lines.text: One who sends a message by the hand of a fool is cutting off feet and drinking violence.
He is cutting off feet, he is drinking injury, Who is sending things by the hand of a fool.

26.he: דַּלְי֣וּ שֹׁ֭קַיִם מִפִּסֵּ֑חַ וּ֝מָשָׁ֗ל בְּפִ֣י כְסִילִֽים׃

lines.text: Like the legs of the lame that hang loose, so is a parable in the mouth of fools.
Weak have been the two legs of the lame, And a parable in the mouth of fools.

26.he: כִּצְר֣וֹר אֶ֭בֶן בְּמַרְגֵּמָ֑ה כֵּן־נוֹתֵ֖ן לִכְסִ֣יל כָּבֽוֹד׃

lines.text: As one who binds a stone in a sling, so is he who gives honor to a fool.
As one who is binding a stone in a sling, So [is] he who is giving honour to a fool.

26.he: ח֭וֹחַ עָלָ֣ה בְיַד־שִׁכּ֑וֹר וּ֝מָשָׁ֗ל בְּפִ֣י כְסִילִֽים׃

lines.text: Like a thorn bush that goes into the hand of a drunkard, so is a parable in the mouth of fools.
A thorn hath gone up into the hand of a drunkard, And a parable in the mouth of fools.

26.he: רַ֥ב מְחֽוֹלֵֽל־כֹּ֑ל וְשֹׂכֵ֥ר כְּ֝סִ֗יל וְשֹׂכֵ֥ר עֹבְרִֽים׃

lines.text: As an archer who wounds all, so is he who hires a fool or he who hires those who pass by.
Great [is] the Former of all, And He is rewarding a fool, And is rewarding transgressors.

26.he: כְּ֭כֶלֶב שָׁ֣ב עַל־קֵא֑וֹ כְּ֝סִ֗יל שׁוֹנֶ֥ה בְאִוַּלְתּֽוֹ׃

lines.text: As a dog that returns to his vomit, so is a fool who repeats his folly.
As a dog hath returned to its vomit, A fool is repeating his folly.

26.he: רָאִ֗יתָ אִ֭ישׁ חָכָ֣ם בְּעֵינָ֑יו תִּקְוָ֖ה לִכְסִ֣יל מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

lines.text: Do you see a man wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
Thou hast seen a man wise in his own eyes, More hope of a fool than of him!

26.he: אָמַ֣ר עָ֭צֵל שַׁ֣חַל בַּדָּ֑רֶךְ אֲ֝רִ֗י בֵּ֣ין הָרְחֹבֽוֹת׃

lines.text: The sluggard says, “There is a lion in the road! A fierce lion roams the streets!”
The slothful hath said, 'A lion [is] in the way, A lion [is] in the broad places.'

26.he: הַ֭דֶּלֶת תִּסּ֣וֹב עַל־צִירָ֑הּ וְ֝עָצֵ֗ל עַל־מִטָּתֽוֹ׃

lines.text: As the door turns on its hinges, so does the sluggard on his bed.
The door turneth round on its hinge, And the slothful on his bed.

26.he: טָ֘מַ֤ן עָצֵ֣ל יָ֭דוֹ בַּצַּלָּ֑חַת נִ֝לְאָ֗ה לַֽהֲשִׁיבָ֥הּ אֶל־פִּֽיו׃

lines.text: The sluggard buries his hand in the dish. He is too lazy to bring it back to his mouth.
The slothful hath hid his hand in a dish, He is weary of bringing it back to his mouth.

26.he: חָכָ֣ם עָצֵ֣ל בְּעֵינָ֑יו מִ֝שִּׁבְעָ֗ה מְשִׁ֣יבֵי טָֽעַם׃

lines.text: The sluggard is wiser in his own eyes than seven men who answer with discretion.
Wiser [is] the slothful in his own eyes, Than seven [men] returning a reason.

26.he: מַחֲזִ֥יק בְּאָזְנֵי־כָ֑לֶב עֹבֵ֥ר מִ֝תְעַבֵּ֗ר עַל־רִ֥יב לֹּֽא־לֽוֹ׃

lines.text: Like one who grabs a dog’s ears is one who passes by and meddles in a quarrel not his own.
Laying hold on the ears of a dog, [Is] a passer-by making himself wrath for strife not his own.

26.he: כְּֽ֭מִתְלַהְלֵהַּ הַיֹּרֶ֥ה זִקִּ֗ים חִצִּ֥ים וָמָֽוֶת׃

lines.text: Like a madman who shoots torches, arrows, and death,
As [one] pretending to be feeble, Who is casting sparks, arrows, and death,

26.he: כֵּֽן־אִ֭ישׁ רִמָּ֣ה אֶת־רֵעֵ֑הוּ וְ֝אָמַ֗ר הֲֽלֹא־מְשַׂחֵ֥ק אָֽנִי׃

lines.text: is the man who deceives his neighbor and says, “Am I not joking?”
So hath a man deceived his neighbour, And hath said, 'Am not I playing?'

26.he: בְּאֶ֣פֶס עֵ֭צִים תִּכְבֶּה־אֵ֑שׁ וּבְאֵ֥ין נִ֝רְגָּ֗ן יִשְׁתֹּ֥ק מָדֽוֹן׃

lines.text: For lack of wood a fire goes out. Without gossip, a quarrel dies down.
Without wood is fire going out, And without a tale-bearer, contention ceaseth,

26.he: פֶּחָ֣ם לְ֭גֶחָלִים וְעֵצִ֣ים לְאֵ֑שׁ וְאִ֥ישׁ מדונים לְחַרְחַר־רִֽיב׃

lines.text: As coals are to hot embers, and wood to fire, so is a contentious man to kindling strife.
Coal to burning coals, and wood to fire, And a man of contentions to kindle strife.

26.he: דִּבְרֵ֣י נִ֭רְגָּן כְּמִֽתְלַהֲמִ֑ים וְ֝הֵ֗ם יָרְד֥וּ חַדְרֵי־בָֽטֶן׃

lines.text: The words of a whisperer are as dainty morsels, they go down into the innermost parts.
The words of a tale-bearer [are] as self-inflicted wounds, And they have gone down [to] the inner parts of the heart.

26.he: כֶּ֣סֶף סִ֭יגִים מְצֻפֶּ֣ה עַל־חָ֑רֶשׂ שְׂפָתַ֖יִם דֹּלְקִ֣ים וְלֶב־רָֽע׃

lines.text: Like silver dross on an earthen vessel are the lips of a fervent one with an evil heart.
Silver of dross spread over potsherd, [Are] burning lips and an evil heart.

26.he: בשפתו יִנָּכֵ֣ר שׂוֹנֵ֑א וּ֝בְקִרְבּ֗וֹ יָשִׁ֥ית מִרְמָֽה׃

lines.text: A malicious man disguises himself with his lips, but he harbors evil in his heart.
By his lips doth a hater dissemble, And in his heart he placeth deceit,

26.he: כִּֽי־יְחַנֵּ֣ן ק֭וֹלוֹ אַל־תַּֽאֲמֶן־בּ֑וֹ כִּ֤י שֶׁ֖בַע תּוֹעֵב֣וֹת בְּלִבּֽוֹ׃

lines.text: When his speech is charming, don’t believe him, for there are seven abominations in his heart.
When his voice is gracious trust not in him, For seven abominations [are] in his heart.

26.he: תִּכַּסֶּ֣ה שִׂ֭נְאָה בְּמַשָּׁא֑וֹן תִּגָּלֶ֖ה רָעָת֣וֹ בְקָהָֽל׃

lines.text: His malice may be concealed by deception, but his wickedness will be exposed in the assembly.
Hatred is covered by deceit, Revealed is its wickedness in an assembly.

26.he: כֹּֽרֶה־שַּׁ֭חַת בָּ֣הּ יִפֹּ֑ל וְגֹ֥לֵ֥ל אֶ֝בֶן אֵלָ֥יו תָּשֽׁוּב׃

lines.text: Whoever digs a pit shall fall into it. Whoever rolls a stone, it will come back on him.
Whoso is digging a pit falleth into it, And the roller of a stone, to him it turneth.

26.he: לְֽשׁוֹן־שֶׁ֭קֶר יִשְׂנָ֣א דַכָּ֑יו וּפֶ֥ה חָ֝לָ֗ק יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה מִדְחֶֽה׃

lines.text: A lying tongue hates those it hurts; and a flattering mouth works ruin.
A lying tongue hateth its bruised ones, And a flattering mouth worketh an overthrow!

27.he: אַֽל־תִּ֭תְהַלֵּל בְּי֣וֹם מָחָ֑ר כִּ֤י לֹא־תֵ֝דַ֗ע מַה־יֵּ֥לֶד יֽוֹם׃

lines.text: Don’t boast about tomorrow; for you don’t know what a day may bring.
Boast not thyself of to-morrow, For thou knowest not what a day bringeth forth.

27.he: יְהַלֶּלְךָ֣ זָ֣ר וְלֹא־פִ֑יךָ נָ֝כְרִ֗י וְאַל־שְׂפָתֶֽיךָ׃

lines.text: Let another man praise you, and not your own mouth; a stranger, and not your own lips.
Let another praise thee, and not thine own mouth, A stranger, and not thine own lips.

27.he: כֹּֽבֶד־אֶ֭בֶן וְנֵ֣טֶל הַח֑וֹל וְכַ֥עַס אֱ֝וִ֗יל כָּבֵ֥ד מִשְּׁנֵיהֶֽם׃

lines.text: A stone is heavy, and sand is a burden; but a fool’s provocation is heavier than both.
A stone [is] heavy, and the sand [is] heavy, And the anger of a fool Is heavier than they both.

27.he: אַכְזְרִיּ֣וּת חֵ֭מָה וְשֶׁ֣טֶף אָ֑ף וּמִ֥י יַ֝עֲמֹד לִפְנֵ֥י קִנְאָֽה׃

lines.text: Wrath is cruel, and anger is overwhelming; but who is able to stand before jealousy?
Fury [is] fierce, and anger [is] overflowing, And who standeth before jealousy?

27.he: ט֭וֹבָה תּוֹכַ֣חַת מְגֻלָּ֑ה מֵֽאַהֲבָ֥ה מְסֻתָּֽרֶת׃

lines.text: Better is open rebuke than hidden love.
Better [is] open reproof than hidden love.

27.he: נֶ֭אֱמָנִים פִּצְעֵ֣י אוֹהֵ֑ב וְ֝נַעְתָּר֗וֹת נְשִׁיק֥וֹת שׂוֹנֵֽא׃

lines.text: The wounds of a friend are faithful, although the kisses of an enemy are profuse.
Faithful are the wounds of a lover, And abundant the kisses of an enemy.

27.he: נֶ֣פֶשׁ שְׂ֭בֵעָה תָּב֣וּס נֹ֑פֶת וְנֶ֥פֶשׁ רְ֝עֵבָ֗ה כָּל־מַ֥ר מָתֽוֹק׃

lines.text: A full soul loathes a honeycomb; but to a hungry soul, every bitter thing is sweet.
A satiated soul treadeth down a honeycomb, And [to] a hungry soul every bitter thing [is] sweet.

27.he: כְּ֭צִפּוֹר נוֹדֶ֣דֶת מִן־קִנָּ֑הּ כֵּֽן־אִ֝֗ישׁ נוֹדֵ֥ד מִמְּקוֹמֽוֹ׃

lines.text: As a bird that wanders from her nest, so is a man who wanders from his home.
As a bird wandering from her nest, So [is] a man wandering from his place.

27.he: שֶׁ֣מֶן וּ֭קְטֹרֶת יְשַׂמַּֽח־לֵ֑ב וּמֶ֥תֶק רֵ֝עֵ֗הוּ מֵֽעֲצַת־נָֽפֶשׁ׃

lines.text: Perfume and incense bring joy to the heart; so does earnest counsel from a man’s friend.
Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart, And the sweetness of one's friend — from counsel of the soul.

27.he: רֵ֥עֲךָ֨ ורעה אָבִ֡יךָ אַֽל־תַּעֲזֹ֗ב וּבֵ֥ית אָחִ֗יךָ אַל־תָּ֭בוֹא בְּי֣וֹם אֵידֶ֑ךָ ט֥וֹב שָׁכֵ֥ן קָ֝ר֗וֹב מֵאָ֥ח רָחֽוֹק׃

lines.text: Don’t forsake your friend and your father’s friend. Don’t go to your brother’s house in the day of your disaster. A neighbor who is near is better than a distant brother.
Thine own friend, and the friend of thy father, forsake not, And the house of thy brother enter not In a day of thy calamity, Better [is] a near neighbour than a brother afar off.

27.he: חֲכַ֣ם בְּ֭נִי וְשַׂמַּ֣ח לִבִּ֑י וְאָשִׁ֖יבָה חֹרְפִ֣י דָבָֽר׃

lines.text: Be wise, my son, and bring joy to my heart, then I can answer my tormentor.
Be wise, my son, and rejoice my heart. And I return my reproacher a word.

27.he: עָר֤וּם רָאָ֣ה רָעָ֣ה נִסְתָּ֑ר פְּ֝תָאיִ֗ם עָבְר֥וּ נֶעֱנָֽשׁוּ׃

lines.text: A prudent man sees danger and takes refuge; but the simple pass on, and suffer for it.
The prudent hath seen the evil, he is hidden, The simple have passed on, they are punished.

27.he: קַח־בִּ֭גְדוֹ כִּי־עָ֣רַב זָ֑ר וּבְעַ֖ד נָכְרִיָּ֣ה חַבְלֵֽהוּ׃

lines.text: Take his garment when he puts up collateral for a stranger. Hold it for a wayward woman!
Take his garment, when a stranger hath been surety, And for a strange woman pledge it.

27.he: מְבָ֘רֵ֤ךְ רֵעֵ֨הוּ ׀ בְּק֣וֹל גָּ֭דוֹל בַּבֹּ֣קֶר הַשְׁכֵּ֑ים קְ֝לָלָ֗ה תֵּחָ֥שֶׁב לֽוֹ׃

lines.text: He who blesses his neighbor with a loud voice early in the morning, it will be taken as a curse by him.
Whoso is saluting his friend with a loud voice, In the morning rising early, A light thing it is reckoned to him.

27.he: דֶּ֣לֶף ט֭וֹרֵד בְּי֣וֹם סַגְרִ֑יר וְאֵ֥שֶׁת מדונים נִשְׁתָּוָֽה׃

lines.text: A continual dropping on a rainy day and a contentious wife are alike:
A continual dropping in a day of rain, And a woman of contentions are alike,

27.he: צֹפְנֶ֥יהָ צָֽפַן־ר֑וּחַ וְשֶׁ֖מֶן יְמִינ֣וֹ יִקְרָֽא׃

lines.text: restraining her is like restraining the wind, or like grasping oil in his right hand.
Whoso is hiding her hath hidden the wind, And the ointment of his right hand calleth out.

27.he: בַּרְזֶ֣ל בְּבַרְזֶ֣ל יָ֑חַד וְ֝אִ֗ישׁ יַ֣חַד פְּנֵֽי־רֵעֵֽהוּ׃

lines.text: Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.
Iron by iron is sharpened, And a man sharpens the face of his friend.

27.he: נֹצֵ֣ר תְּ֭אֵנָה יֹאכַ֣ל פִּרְיָ֑הּ וְשֹׁמֵ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣יו יְכֻבָּֽד׃

lines.text: Whoever tends the fig tree shall eat its fruit. He who looks after his master shall be honored.
The keeper of a fig-tree eateth its fruit, And the preserver of his master is honoured.

27.he: כַּ֭מַּיִם הַפָּנִ֣ים לַפָּנִ֑ים כֵּ֤ן לֵֽב־הָ֝אָדָ֗ם לָאָדָֽם׃

lines.text: Like water reflects a face, so a man’s heart reflects the man.
As [in] water the face [is] to face, So the heart of man to man.

27.he: שְׁא֣וֹל ואבדה לֹ֣א תִשְׂבַּ֑עְנָה וְעֵינֵ֥י הָ֝אָדָ֗ם לֹ֣א תִשְׂבַּֽעְנָה׃

lines.text: Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; and a man’s eyes are never satisfied.
Sheol and destruction are not satisfied, And the eyes of man are not satisfied.

27.he: מַצְרֵ֣ף לַ֭כֶּסֶף וְכ֣וּר לַזָּהָ֑ב וְ֝אִ֗ישׁ לְפִ֣י מַהֲלָלֽוֹ׃

lines.text: The crucible is for silver, and the furnace for gold; but man is refined by his praise.
A refining pot [is] for silver, and a furnace for gold, And a man according to his praise.

27.he: אִ֥ם תִּכְתּֽוֹשׁ־אֶת־הָאֱוִ֨יל ׀ בַּֽמַּכְתֵּ֡שׁ בְּת֣וֹךְ הָ֭רִיפוֹת בַּֽעֱלִ֑י לֹא־תָס֥וּר מֵ֝עָלָ֗יו אִוַּלְתּֽוֹ׃

lines.text: Though you grind a fool in a mortar with a pestle along with grain, yet his foolishness will not be removed from him.
If thou dost beat the foolish in a mortar, Among washed things — with a pestle, His folly turneth not aside from off him.

27.he: יָדֹ֣עַ תֵּ֭דַע פְּנֵ֣י צֹאנֶ֑ךָ שִׁ֥ית לִ֝בְּךָ֗ לַעֲדָרִֽים׃

lines.text: Know well the state of your flocks, and pay attention to your herds:
Know well the face of thy flock, Set thy heart to the droves,

27.he: כִּ֤י לֹ֣א לְעוֹלָ֣ם חֹ֑סֶן וְאִם־נֵ֝֗זֶר לְד֣וֹר דור׃

lines.text: for riches are not forever, nor does the crown endure to all generations.
For riches [are] not to the age, Nor a crown to generation and generation.

27.he: גָּלָ֣ה חָ֭צִיר וְנִרְאָה־דֶ֑שֶׁא וְ֝נֶאֶסְפ֗וּ עִשְּׂב֥וֹת הָרִֽים׃

lines.text: The hay is removed, and the new growth appears, the grasses of the hills are gathered in.
Revealed was the hay, and seen the tender grass, And gathered the herbs of mountains.

27.he: כְּבָשִׂ֥ים לִלְבוּשֶׁ֑ךָ וּמְחִ֥יר שָׂ֝דֶ֗ה עַתּוּדִֽים׃

lines.text: The lambs are for your clothing, and the goats are the price of a field.
Lambs [are] for thy clothing, And the price of the field [are] he-goats,

27.he: וְדֵ֤י ׀ חֲלֵ֬ב עִזִּ֗ים לְֽ֭לַחְמְךָ לְלֶ֣חֶם בֵּיתֶ֑ךָ וְ֝חַיִּ֗ים לְנַעֲרוֹתֶֽיךָ׃

lines.text: There will be plenty of goats’ milk for your food, for your family’s food, and for the nourishment of your servant girls.
And a sufficiency of goats' milk [is] for thy bread, For bread to thy house, and life to thy damsels!

28.he: נָ֣סוּ וְאֵין־רֹדֵ֣ף רָשָׁ֑ע וְ֝צַדִּיקִ֗ים כִּכְפִ֥יר יִבְטָֽח׃

lines.text: The wicked flee when no one pursues; but the righteous are as bold as a lion.
The wicked have fled and there is no pursuer. And the righteous as a young lion is confident.

28.he: בְּפֶ֣שַֽׁע אֶ֭רֶץ רַבִּ֣ים שָׂרֶ֑יהָ וּבְאָדָ֥ם מֵבִ֥ין יֹ֝דֵ֗עַ כֵּ֣ן יַאֲרִֽיךְ׃

lines.text: In rebellion, a land has many rulers, but order is maintained by a man of understanding and knowledge.
By the transgression of a land many [are] its heads. And by an intelligent man, Who knoweth right — it is prolonged.

28.he: גֶּ֣בֶר רָ֭שׁ וְעֹשֵׁ֣ק דַּלִּ֑ים מָטָ֥ר סֹ֝חֵ֗ף וְאֵ֣ין לָֽחֶם׃

lines.text: A needy man who oppresses the poor is like a driving rain which leaves no crops.
A man — poor and oppressing the weak, [Is] a sweeping rain, and there is no bread.

28.he: עֹזְבֵ֣י ת֭וֹרָה יְהַֽלְל֣וּ רָשָׁ֑ע וְשֹׁמְרֵ֥י ת֝וֹרָ֗ה יִתְגָּ֥רוּ בָֽם׃

lines.text: Those who forsake the law praise the wicked; but those who keep the law contend with them.
Those forsaking the law praise the wicked, Those keeping the law plead against them.

28.he: אַנְשֵׁי־רָ֭ע לֹא־יָבִ֣ינוּ מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּמְבַקְשֵׁ֥י יְ֝הוָ֗ה יָבִ֥ינוּ כֹֽל׃

lines.text: Evil men don’t understand justice; but those who seek Yahweh understand it fully.
Evil men understand not judgment, And those seeking Jehovah understand all.

28.he: טֽוֹב־רָ֭שׁ הוֹלֵ֣ךְ בְּתֻמּ֑וֹ מֵעִקֵּ֥שׁ דְּ֝רָכַ֗יִם וְה֣וּא עָשִֽׁיר׃

lines.text: Better is the poor who walks in his integrity, than he who is perverse in his ways, and he is rich.
Better [is] the poor walking in his integrity, Than the perverse of ways who is rich.

28.he: נוֹצֵ֣ר תּ֭וֹרָה בֵּ֣ן מֵבִ֑ין וְרֹעֶה זֽ֝וֹלְלִ֗ים יַכְלִ֥ים אָבִֽיו׃

lines.text: Whoever keeps the law is a wise son; but he who is a companion of gluttons shames his father.
Whoso is keeping the law is an intelligent son, And a friend of gluttons, Doth cause his father to blush.

28.he: מַרְבֶּ֣ה ה֭וֹנוֹ בְּנֶ֣שֶׁךְ ובתרבית לְחוֹנֵ֖ן דַּלִּ֣ים יִקְבְּצֶֽנּוּ׃

lines.text: He who increases his wealth by excessive interest gathers it for one who has pity on the poor.
Whoso is multiplying his wealth by biting and usury, For one favouring the poor doth gather it.

28.he: מֵסִ֣יר אָ֭זְנוֹ מִשְּׁמֹ֣עַ תּוֹרָ֑ה גַּ֥ם־תְּ֝פִלָּת֗וֹ תּוֹעֵבָֽה׃

lines.text: He who turns away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer is an abomination.
Whoso is turning his ear from hearing the law, Even his prayer [is] an abomination.

28.he: מַשְׁגֶּ֤ה יְשָׁרִ֨ים ׀ בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ רָ֗ע בִּשְׁחוּת֥וֹ הֽוּא־יִפּ֑וֹל וּ֝תְמִימִ֗ים יִנְחֲלוּ־טֽוֹב׃

lines.text: Whoever causes the upright to go astray in an evil way, he will fall into his own trap; but the blameless will inherit good.
Whoso is causing the upright to err in an evil way, Into his own pit he doth fall, And the perfect do inherit good.

28.he: חָכָ֣ם בְּ֭עֵינָיו אִ֣ישׁ עָשִׁ֑יר וְדַ֖ל מֵבִ֣ין יַחְקְרֶֽנּוּ׃

lines.text: The rich man is wise in his own eyes; but the poor who has understanding sees through him.
A rich man is wise in his own eyes, And the intelligent poor searcheth him.

28.he: בַּעֲלֹ֣ץ צַ֭דִּיקִים רַבָּ֣ה תִפְאָ֑רֶת וּבְק֥וּם רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים יְחֻפַּ֥שׂ אָדָֽם׃

lines.text: When the righteous triumph, there is great glory; but when the wicked rise, men hide themselves.
In the exulting of the righteous the glory [is] abundant, And in the rising of the wicked man is apprehensive.

28.he: מְכַסֶּ֣ה פְ֭שָׁעָיו לֹ֣א יַצְלִ֑יחַ וּמוֹדֶ֖ה וְעֹזֵ֣ב יְרֻחָֽם׃

lines.text: He who conceals his sins doesn’t prosper, but whoever confesses and renounces them finds mercy.
Whoso is covering his transgressions prospereth not, And he who is confessing and forsaking hath mercy.

28.he: אַשְׁרֵ֣י אָ֭דָם מְפַחֵ֣ד תָּמִ֑יד וּמַקְשֶׁ֥ה לִ֝בּ֗וֹ יִפּ֥וֹל בְּרָעָֽה׃

lines.text: Blessed is the man who always fears; but one who hardens his heart falls into trouble.
O the happiness of a man fearing continually, And whoso is hardening his heart falleth into evil.

28.he: אֲרִי־נֹ֭הֵם וְדֹ֣ב שׁוֹקֵ֑ק מֹשֵׁ֥ל רָ֝שָׁ֗ע עַ֣ל עַם־דָּֽל׃

lines.text: As a roaring lion or a charging bear, so is a wicked ruler over helpless people.
A growling lion, and a ranging bear, [Is] the wicked ruler over a poor people.

28.he: נָגִ֗יד חֲסַ֣ר תְּ֭בוּנוֹת וְרַ֥ב מַעֲשַׁקּ֑וֹת שנאי בֶ֝֗צַע יַאֲרִ֥יךְ יָמִֽים׃

lines.text: A tyrannical ruler lacks judgment. One who hates ill-gotten gain will have long days.
A leader lacking understanding multiplieth oppressions, Whoso is hating dishonest gain prolongeth days.

28.he: אָ֭דָם עָשֻׁ֣ק בְּדַם־נָפֶשׁ עַד־בּ֥וֹר יָ֝נ֗וּס אַל־יִתְמְכוּ־בֽוֹ׃

lines.text: A man who is tormented by life blood will be a fugitive until death; no one will support him.
A man oppressed with the blood of a soul, Unto the pit fleeth, none taketh hold on him.

28.he: הוֹלֵ֣ךְ תָּ֭מִים יִוָּשֵׁ֑עַ וְנֶעְקַ֥שׁ דְּ֝רָכַ֗יִם יִפּ֥וֹל בְּאֶחָֽת׃

lines.text: Whoever walks blamelessly is kept safe; but one with perverse ways will fall suddenly.
Whoso is walking uprightly is saved, And the perverted of ways falleth at once.

28.he: עֹבֵ֣ד אַ֭דְמָתוֹ יִֽשְׂבַּֽע־לָ֑חֶם וּמְרַדֵּ֥ף רֵ֝קִ֗ים יִֽשְׂבַּֽע־רִֽישׁ׃

lines.text: One who works his land will have an abundance of food; but one who chases fantasies will have his fill of poverty.
Whoso is tilling his ground is satisfied [with] bread, And whoso is pursuing vanity, Is filled [with] poverty.

28.he: אִ֣ישׁ אֱ֭מוּנוֹת רַב־בְּרָכ֑וֹת וְאָ֥ץ לְ֝הַעֲשִׁ֗יר לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶֽה׃

lines.text: A faithful man is rich with blessings; but one who is eager to be rich will not go unpunished.
A stedfast man hath multiplied blessings, And whoso is hasting to be rich is not acquitted.

28.he: הַֽכֵּר־פָּנִ֥ים לֹא־ט֑וֹב וְעַל־פַּת־לֶ֝֗חֶם יִפְשַׁע־גָּֽבֶר׃

lines.text: To show partiality is not good; yet a man will do wrong for a piece of bread.
To discern faces is not good, And for a piece of bread doth a man transgress.

28.he: נִֽבֳהָ֥ל לַה֗וֹן אִ֭ישׁ רַ֣ע עָ֑יִן וְלֹֽא־יֵ֝דַע כִּי־חֶ֥סֶר יְבֹאֶֽנּוּ׃

lines.text: A stingy man hurries after riches, and doesn’t know that poverty waits for him.
Troubled for wealth [is] the man [with] an evil eye, And he knoweth not that want doth meet him.

28.he: מ֘וֹכִ֤יחַ אָדָ֣ם אַ֭חֲרַי חֵ֣ן יִמְצָ֑א מִֽמַּחֲלִ֥יק לָשֽׁוֹן׃

lines.text: One who rebukes a man will afterward find more favor than one who flatters with the tongue.
Whoso is reproving a man afterwards findeth grace, More than a flatterer with the tongue.

28.he: גּוֹזֵ֤ל ׀ אָ֘בִ֤יו וְאִמּ֗וֹ וְאֹמֵ֥ר אֵֽין־פָּ֑שַׁע חָבֵ֥ר ה֝֗וּא לְאִ֣ישׁ מַשְׁחִֽית׃

lines.text: Whoever robs his father or his mother and says, “It’s not wrong,” is a partner with a destroyer.
Whoso is robbing his father, or his mother, And is saying, 'It is not transgression,' A companion he is to a destroyer.

28.he: רְחַב־נֶ֭פֶשׁ יְגָרֶ֣ה מָד֑וֹן וּבוֹטֵ֖חַ עַל־יְהוָ֣ה יְדֻשָּֽׁן׃

lines.text: One who is greedy stirs up strife; but one who trusts in Yahweh will prosper.
Whoso is proud in soul stirreth up contention, And whoso is trusting on Jehovah is made fat.

28.he: בּוֹטֵ֣חַ בְּ֭לִבּוֹ ה֣וּא כְסִ֑יל וְהוֹלֵ֥ךְ בְּ֝חָכְמָ֗ה ה֣וּא יִמָּלֵֽט׃

lines.text: One who trusts in himself is a fool; but one who walks in wisdom is kept safe.
Whoso is trusting in his heart is a fool, And whoso is walking in wisdom is delivered.

28.he: נוֹתֵ֣ן לָ֭רָשׁ אֵ֣ין מַחְס֑וֹר וּמַעְלִ֥ים עֵ֝ינָ֗יו רַב־מְאֵרֽוֹת׃

lines.text: One who gives to the poor has no lack; but one who closes his eyes will have many curses.
Whoso is giving to the poor hath no lack, And whoso is hiding his eyes multiplied curses.

28.he: בְּק֣וּם רְ֭שָׁעִים יִסָּתֵ֣ר אָדָ֑ם וּ֝בְאָבְדָ֗ם יִרְבּ֥וּ צַדִּיקִֽים׃

lines.text: When the wicked rise, men hide themselves; but when they perish, the righteous thrive.
In the rising of the wicked a man is hidden, And in their destruction the righteous multiply!

29.he: אִ֣ישׁ תּ֭וֹכָחוֹת מַקְשֶׁה־עֹ֑רֶף פֶּ֥תַע יִ֝שָּׁבֵ֗ר וְאֵ֣ין מַרְפֵּֽא׃

lines.text: He who is often rebuked and stiffens his neck will be destroyed suddenly, with no remedy.
A man often reproved, hardening the neck, Is suddenly broken, and there is no healing.

29.he: בִּרְב֣וֹת צַ֭דִּיקִים יִשְׂמַ֣ח הָעָ֑ם וּבִמְשֹׁ֥ל רָ֝שָׁ֗ע יֵאָ֥נַֽח עָֽם׃

lines.text: When the righteous thrive, the people rejoice; but when the wicked rule, the people groan.
In the multiplying of the righteous the people rejoice, And in the ruling of the wicked the people sigh.

29.he: אִֽישׁ־אֹהֵ֣ב חָ֭כְמָה יְשַׂמַּ֣ח אָבִ֑יו וְרֹעֶ֥ה ז֝וֹנ֗וֹת יְאַבֶּד־הֽוֹן׃

lines.text: Whoever loves wisdom brings joy to his father; but a companion of prostitutes squanders his wealth.
A man loving wisdom rejoiceth his father, And a friend of harlots destroyeth wealth.

29.he: מֶ֗לֶךְ בְּ֭מִשְׁפָּט יַעֲמִ֣יד אָ֑רֶץ וְאִ֖ישׁ תְּרוּמ֣וֹת יֶֽהֶרְסֶֽנָּה׃

lines.text: The king by justice makes the land stable, but he who takes bribes tears it down.
A king by judgment establisheth a land, And one receiving gifts throweth it down.

29.he: גֶּ֭בֶר מַחֲלִ֣יק עַל־רֵעֵ֑הוּ רֶ֝֗שֶׁת פּוֹרֵ֥שׂ עַל־פְּעָמָֽיו׃

lines.text: A man who flatters his neighbor spreads a net for his feet.
A man taking a portion above his neighbour, Spreadeth a net for his own steps.

29.he: בְּפֶ֤שַֽׁע אִ֣ישׁ רָ֣ע מוֹקֵ֑שׁ וְ֝צַדִּ֗יק יָר֥וּן וְשָׂמֵֽחַ׃

lines.text: An evil man is snared by his sin, but the righteous can sing and be glad.
In the transgression of the evil [is] a snare, And the righteous doth sing and rejoice.

29.he: יֹדֵ֣עַ צַ֭דִּיק דִּ֣ין דַּלִּ֑ים רָ֝שָׁ֗ע לֹא־יָבִ֥ין דָּֽעַת׃

lines.text: The righteous care about justice for the poor. The wicked aren’t concerned about knowledge.
The righteous knoweth the plea of the poor, The wicked understandeth not knowledge.

29.he: אַנְשֵׁ֣י לָ֭צוֹן יָפִ֣יחוּ קִרְיָ֑ה וַ֝חֲכָמִ֗ים יָשִׁ֥יבוּ אָֽף׃

lines.text: Mockers stir up a city, but wise men turn away anger.
Men of scorning ensnare a city, And the wise turn back anger.

29.he: אִֽישׁ־חָכָ֗ם נִ֭שְׁפָּט אֶת־אִ֣ישׁ אֱוִ֑יל וְרָגַ֥ז וְ֝שָׂחַ֗ק וְאֵ֣ין נָֽחַת׃

lines.text: If a wise man goes to court with a foolish man, the fool rages or scoffs, and there is no peace.
A wise man is judged by the foolish man, And he hath been angry, And he hath laughed, and there is no rest.

29.he: אַנְשֵׁ֣י דָ֭מִים יִשְׂנְאוּ־תָ֑ם וִֽ֝ישָׁרִ֗ים יְבַקְשׁ֥וּ נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃

lines.text: The bloodthirsty hate a man of integrity; and they seek the life of the upright.
Men of blood hate the perfect, And the upright seek his soul.

29.he: כָּל־ר֭וּחוֹ יוֹצִ֣יא כְסִ֑יל וְ֝חָכָ֗ם בְּאָח֥וֹר יְשַׁבְּחֶֽנָּה׃

lines.text: A fool vents all of his anger, but a wise man brings himself under control.
A fool bringeth out all his mind, And the wise till afterwards restraineth it.

29.he: מֹ֭שֵׁל מַקְשִׁ֣יב עַל־דְּבַר־שָׁ֑קֶר כָּֽל־מְשָׁרְתָ֥יו רְשָׁעִֽים׃

lines.text: If a ruler listens to lies, all of his officials are wicked.
A ruler who is attending to lying words, All his ministers [are] wicked.

29.he: רָ֤שׁ וְאִ֣ישׁ תְּכָכִ֣ים נִפְגָּ֑שׁוּ מֵ֤אִיר־עֵינֵ֖י שְׁנֵיהֶ֣ם יְהוָֽה׃

lines.text: The poor man and the oppressor have this in common: Yahweh gives sight to the eyes of both.
The poor and the man of frauds have met together, Jehovah is enlightening the eyes of them both.

29.he: מֶ֤לֶךְ שׁוֹפֵ֣ט בֶּֽאֱמֶ֣ת דַּלִּ֑ים כִּ֝סְא֗וֹ לָעַ֥ד יִכּֽוֹן׃

lines.text: The king who fairly judges the poor, his throne shall be established forever.
a king that is judging truly the poor, His throne for ever is established.

29.he: שֵׁ֣בֶט וְ֭תוֹכַחַת יִתֵּ֣ן חָכְמָ֑ה וְנַ֥עַר מְ֝שֻׁלָּ֗ח מֵבִ֥ישׁ אִמּֽוֹ׃

lines.text: The rod of correction gives wisdom, but a child left to himself causes shame to his mother.
A rod and reproof give wisdom, And a youth let away is shaming his mother.

29.he: בִּרְב֣וֹת רְ֭שָׁעִים יִרְבֶּה־פָּ֑שַׁע וְ֝צַדִּיקִ֗ים בְּֽמַפַּלְתָּ֥ם יִרְאֽוּ׃

lines.text: When the wicked increase, sin increases; but the righteous will see their downfall.
In the multiplying of the wicked transgression multiplieth, And the righteous on their fall do look.

29.he: יַסֵּ֣ר בִּ֭נְךָ וִֽינִיחֶ֑ךָ וְיִתֵּ֖ן מַעֲדַנִּ֣ים לְנַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃

lines.text: Correct your son, and he will give you peace; yes, he will bring delight to your soul.
Chastise thy son, and he giveth thee comfort, Yea, he giveth delights to thy soul.

29.he: בְּאֵ֣ין חָ֭זוֹן יִפָּ֣רַֽע עָ֑ם וְשֹׁמֵ֖ר תּוֹרָ֣ה אַשְׁרֵֽהוּ׃

lines.text: Where there is no revelation, the people cast off restraint; but one who keeps the law is blessed.
Without a Vision is a people made naked, And whoso is keeping the law, O his happiness!

29.he: בִּ֭דְבָרִים לֹא־יִוָּ֣סֶר עָ֑בֶד כִּֽי־יָ֝בִ֗ין וְאֵ֣ין מַעֲנֶֽה׃

lines.text: A servant can’t be corrected by words. Though he understands, yet he will not respond.
By words a servant is not instructed though he understand, And there is nothing answering.

29.he: חָזִ֗יתָ אִ֭ישׁ אָ֣ץ בִּדְבָרָ֑יו תִּקְוָ֖ה לִכְסִ֣יל מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

lines.text: Do you see a man who is hasty in his words? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
Thou hast seen a man hasty in his words! More hope of a fool than of him.

29.he: מְפַנֵּ֣ק מִנֹּ֣עַר עַבְדּ֑וֹ וְ֝אַחֲרִית֗וֹ יִהְיֶ֥ה מָנֽוֹן׃

lines.text: He who pampers his servant from youth will have him become a son in the end.
Whoso is bringing up his servant delicately, from youth, [At] his latter end also he is continuator.

29.he: אִֽישׁ־אַ֭ף יְגָרֶ֣ה מָד֑וֹן וּבַ֖עַל חֵמָ֣ה רַב־פָּֽשַׁע׃

lines.text: An angry man stirs up strife, and a wrathful man abounds in sin.
An angry man stirreth up contention, And a furious man is multiplying transgression.

29.he: גַּאֲוַ֣ת אָ֭דָם תַּשְׁפִּילֶ֑נּוּ וּשְׁפַל־ר֝֗וּחַ יִתְמֹ֥ךְ כָּבֽוֹד׃

lines.text: A man’s pride brings him low, but one of lowly spirit gains honor.
The pride of man humbleth him, And humility of spirit upholdeth honour.

29.he: חוֹלֵ֣ק עִם־גַּ֭נָּב שׂוֹנֵ֣א נַּפְשׁ֑וֹ אָלָ֥ה יִ֝שְׁמַ֗ע וְלֹ֣א יַגִּֽיד׃

lines.text: Whoever is an accomplice of a thief is an enemy of his own soul. He takes an oath, but dares not testify.
Whoso is sharing with a thief is hating his own soul, Execration he heareth, and telleth not.

29.he: חֶרְדַּ֣ת אָ֭דָם יִתֵּ֣ן מוֹקֵ֑שׁ וּבוֹטֵ֖חַ בַּיהוָ֣ה יְשֻׂגָּֽב׃

lines.text: The fear of man proves to be a snare, but whoever puts his trust in Yahweh is kept safe.
Fear of man causeth a snare, And the confident in Jehovah is set on high.

29.he: רַ֭בִּים מְבַקְשִׁ֣ים פְּנֵי־מוֹשֵׁ֑ל וּ֝מֵיְהוָ֗ה מִשְׁפַּט־אִֽישׁ׃

lines.text: Many seek the ruler’s favor, but a man’s justice comes from Yahweh.
Many are seeking the face of a ruler, And from Jehovah [is] the judgment of each.

29.he: תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת צַ֭דִּיקִים אִ֣ישׁ עָ֑וֶל וְתוֹעֲבַ֖ת רָשָׁ֣ע יְשַׁר־דָּֽרֶךְ׃

lines.text: A dishonest man detests the righteous, and the upright in their ways detest the wicked.
An abomination to the righteous [is] the perverse man, And an abomination to the wicked [is] the upright in the way!

30.he: דִּבְרֵ֤י ׀ אָג֥וּר בִּן־יָקֶ֗ה הַמַּ֫שָּׂ֥א נְאֻ֣ם הַ֭גֶּבֶר לְאִֽיתִיאֵ֑ל לְאִ֖יתִיאֵ֣ל וְאֻכָֽל׃

lines.text: The words of Agur the son of Jakeh; the revelation: the man says to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal:
Words of a Gatherer, son of an obedient one, the declaration, an affirmation of the man: — I have wearied myself [for] God, I have wearied myself [for] God, and am consumed.

30.he: כִּ֤י בַ֣עַר אָנֹכִ֣י מֵאִ֑ישׁ וְלֹֽא־בִינַ֖ת אָדָ֣ם לִֽי׃

lines.text: “Surely I am the most ignorant man, and don’t have a man’s understanding.
For I am more brutish than any one, And have not the understanding of a man.

30.he: וְלֹֽא־לָמַ֥דְתִּי חָכְמָ֑ה וְדַ֖עַת קְדֹשִׁ֣ים אֵדָֽע׃

lines.text: I have not learned wisdom, neither do I have the knowledge of the Holy One.
Nor have I learned wisdom, Yet the knowledge of Holy Ones I know.

30.he: מִ֤י עָלָֽה־שָׁמַ֨יִם ׀ וַיֵּרַ֡ד מִ֤י אָֽסַף־ר֨וּחַ ׀ בְּחָפְנָ֡יו מִ֤י צָֽרַר־מַ֨יִם ׀ בַּשִּׂמְלָ֗ה מִ֭י הֵקִ֣ים כָּל־אַפְסֵי־אָ֑רֶץ מַה־שְּׁמ֥וֹ וּמַֽה־שֶּׁם־בְּ֝נ֗וֹ כִּ֣י תֵדָֽע׃

lines.text: Who has ascended up into heaven, and descended? Who has gathered the wind in his fists? Who has bound the waters in his garment? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is his name, and what is his son’s name, if you know?

Who went up to heaven, and cometh down? Who hath gathered the wind in his fists? Who hath bound waters in a garment? Who established all ends of the earth? What [is] His name? and what His son's name? Surely thou knowest!

30.he: כָּל־אִמְּרַ֣ת אֱל֣וֹהַּ צְרוּפָ֑ה מָגֵ֥ן ה֝֗וּא לַֽחֹסִ֥ים בּֽוֹ׃

lines.text: “Every word of God is flawless. He is a shield to those who take refuge in him.
Every saying of God [is] tried, A shield He [is] to those trusting in Him.

30.he: אַל־תּ֥וֹסְףְּ עַל־דְּבָרָ֑יו פֶּן־יוֹכִ֖יחַ בְּךָ֣ וְנִכְזָֽבְתָּ׃

lines.text: Don’t you add to his words, lest he reprove you, and you be found a liar.
Add not to His words, lest He reason with thee, And thou hast been found false.

30.he: שְׁ֭תַּיִם שָׁאַ֣לְתִּי מֵאִתָּ֑ךְ אַל־תִּמְנַ֥ע מִ֝מֶּ֗נִּי בְּטֶ֣רֶם אָמֽוּת׃

lines.text: “Two things I have asked of you. Don’t deny me before I die.
Two things I have asked from Thee, Withhold not from me before I die.

30.he: שָׁ֤וְא ׀ וּֽדְבַר־כָּזָ֡ב הַרְחֵ֬ק מִמֶּ֗נִּי רֵ֣אשׁ וָ֭עֹשֶׁר אַל־תִּֽתֶּן־לִ֑י הַ֝טְרִיפֵ֗נִי לֶ֣חֶם חֻקִּֽי׃

lines.text: Remove far from me falsehood and lies. Give me neither poverty nor riches. Feed me with the food that is needful for me,
Vanity and a lying word put far from me, Poverty or wealth give not to me, Cause me to eat the bread of my portion,

30.he: פֶּ֥ן אֶשְׂבַּ֨ע ׀ וְכִחַשְׁתִּי֮ וְאָמַ֗רְתִּי מִ֥י יְה֫וָ֥ה וּפֶֽן־אִוָּרֵ֥שׁ וְגָנַ֑בְתִּי וְ֝תָפַ֗שְׂתִּי שֵׁ֣ם אֱלֹהָֽי׃

lines.text: lest I be full, deny you, and say, ‘Who is Yahweh?’ or lest I be poor, and steal, and so dishonor the name of my God.
Lest I become satiated, and have denied, And have said, 'Who [is] Jehovah?' And lest I be poor, and have stolen, And have laid hold of the name of my God.

30.he: אַל־תַּלְשֵׁ֣ן עֶ֭בֶד אֶל־אדנו פֶּֽן־יְקַלֶּלְךָ֥ וְאָשָֽׁמְתָּ׃

lines.text: “Don’t slander a servant to his master, lest he curse you, and you be held guilty.
Accuse not a servant unto his lord, Lest he disesteem thee, and thou be found guilty.

30.he: דּ֭וֹר אָבִ֣יו יְקַלֵּ֑ל וְאֶת־אִ֝מּ֗וֹ לֹ֣א יְבָרֵֽךְ׃

lines.text: There is a generation that curses their father, and doesn’t bless their mother.
A generation [is], that lightly esteemeth their father, And their mother doth not bless.

30.he: דּ֭וֹר טָה֣וֹר בְּעֵינָ֑יו וּ֝מִצֹּאָת֗וֹ לֹ֣א רֻחָֽץ׃

lines.text: There is a generation that is pure in their own eyes, yet are not washed from their filthiness.
A generation — pure in their own eyes, But from their own filth not washed.

30.he: דּ֭וֹר מָה־רָמ֣וּ עֵינָ֑יו וְ֝עַפְעַפָּ֗יו יִנָּשֵֽׂאוּ׃

lines.text: There is a generation, oh how lofty are their eyes! Their eyelids are lifted up.
A generation — how high are their eyes, Yea, their eyelids are lifted up.

30.he: דּ֤וֹר ׀ חֲרָב֣וֹת שִׁנָּיו֮ וּֽמַאֲכָל֪וֹת מְֽתַלְּעֹ֫תָ֥יו לֶאֱכֹ֣ל עֲנִיִּ֣ים מֵאֶ֑רֶץ וְ֝אֶבְיוֹנִ֗ים מֵאָדָֽם׃

lines.text: There is a generation whose teeth are like swords, and their jaws like knives, to devour the poor from the earth, and the needy from among men.
A generation — swords [are] their teeth, And knives — their jaw-teeth, To consume the poor from earth, And the needy from [among] men.

30.he: לַ֥עֲלוּקָ֨ה ׀ שְׁתֵּ֥י בָנוֹת֮ הַ֤ב ׀ הַ֥ב שָׁל֣וֹשׁ הֵ֭נָּה לֹ֣א תִשְׂבַּ֑עְנָה אַ֝רְבַּ֗ע לֹא־אָ֥מְרוּ הֽוֹן׃

lines.text: “The leech has two daughters: ‘Give, give.’ “There are three things that are never satisfied; four that don’t say, ‘Enough:’
To the leech [are] two daughters, 'Give, give, Lo, three things are not satisfied, Four have not said 'Sufficiency;'

30.he: שְׁאוֹל֮ וְעֹ֪צֶ֫ר רָ֥חַם אֶ֭רֶץ לֹא־שָׂ֣בְעָה מַּ֑יִם וְ֝אֵ֗שׁ לֹא־אָ֥מְרָה הֽוֹן׃

lines.text: Sheol, the barren womb; the earth that is not satisfied with water; and the fire that doesn’t say, ‘Enough.’
Sheol, and a restrained womb, Earth — it [is] not satisfied [with] water, And fire — it hath not said, 'Sufficiency,'

30.he: עַ֤יִן ׀ תִּֽלְעַ֣ג לְאָב֮ וְתָב֪וּז לִֽיקֲּהַ֫ת־אֵ֥ם יִקְּר֥וּהָ עֹרְבֵי־נַ֑חַל וְֽיֹאכְל֥וּהָ בְנֵי־נָֽשֶׁר׃

lines.text: “The eye that mocks at his father, and scorns obedience to his mother: the ravens of the valley shall pick it out, the young eagles shall eat it.
An eye that mocketh at a father, And despiseth to obey a mother, Dig it out do ravens of the valley, And eat it do young eagles.

30.he: שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה הֵ֭מָּה נִפְלְא֣וּ מִמֶּ֑נִּי וארבע לֹ֣א יְדַעְתִּֽים׃

lines.text: “There are three things which are too amazing for me, four which I don’t understand:
Three things have been too wonderful for me, Yea, four that I have not known:

30.he: דֶּ֤רֶךְ הַנֶּ֨שֶׁר ׀ בַּשָּׁמַיִם֮ דֶּ֥רֶךְ נָחָ֗שׁ עֲלֵ֫י צ֥וּר דֶּֽרֶךְ־אֳנִיָּ֥ה בְלֶב־יָ֑ם וְדֶ֖רֶךְ גֶּ֣בֶר בְּעַלְמָֽה׃

lines.text: The way of an eagle in the air, the way of a serpent on a rock, the way of a ship in the middle of the sea, and the way of a man with a maiden.
The way of the eagle in the heavens, The way of a serpent on a rock, The way of a ship in the heart of the sea, And the way of a man in youth.

30.he: כֵּ֤ן ׀ דֶּ֥רֶךְ אִשָּׁ֗ה מְנָ֫אָ֥פֶת אָ֭כְלָה וּמָ֣חֲתָה פִ֑יהָ וְ֝אָמְרָ֗ה לֹֽא־פָעַ֥לְתִּי אָֽוֶן׃

lines.text: “So is the way of an adulterous woman: She eats and wipes her mouth, and says, ‘I have done nothing wrong.’
So — the way of an adulterous woman, She hath eaten and hath wiped her mouth, And hath said, 'I have not done iniquity.'

30.he: תַּ֣חַת שָׁ֭לוֹשׁ רָ֣גְזָה אֶ֑רֶץ וְתַ֥חַת אַ֝רְבַּ֗ע לֹא־תוּכַ֥ל שְׂאֵֽת׃

lines.text: “For three things the earth trembles, and under four, it can’t bear up:
For three things hath earth been troubled, And for four — it is not able to bear:

30.he: תַּֽחַת־עֶ֭בֶד כִּ֣י יִמְל֑וֹךְ וְ֝נָבָ֗ל כִּ֣י יִֽשְׂבַּֽע־לָֽחֶם׃

lines.text: For a servant when he is king, a fool when he is filled with food,
For a servant when he reigneth, And a fool when he is satisfied with bread,

30.he: תַּ֣חַת שְׂ֭נוּאָה כִּ֣י תִבָּעֵ֑ל וְ֝שִׁפְחָ֗ה כִּֽי־תִירַ֥שׁ גְּבִרְתָּֽהּ׃

lines.text: for an unloved woman when she is married, and a servant who is heir to her mistress.
For a hated one when she ruleth, And a maid-servant when she succeedeth her mistress.

30.he: אַרְבָּ֣עָה הֵ֭ם קְטַנֵּי־אָ֑רֶץ וְ֝הֵ֗מָּה חֲכָמִ֥ים מְחֻכָּמִֽים׃

lines.text: “There are four things which are little on the earth, but they are exceedingly wise:
Four [are] little ones of earth, And they are made wiser than the wise:

30.he: הַ֭נְּמָלִים עַ֣ם לֹא־עָ֑ז וַיָּכִ֖ינוּ בַקַּ֣יִץ לַחְמָֽם׃

lines.text: The ants are not a strong people, yet they provide their food in the summer.
The ants [are] a people not strong, And they prepare in summer their food,

30.he: שְׁ֭פַנִּים עַ֣ם לֹא־עָצ֑וּם וַיָּשִׂ֖ימוּ בַסֶּ֣לַע בֵּיתָֽם׃

lines.text: The hyraxes are but a feeble folk, yet make they their houses in the rocks.
Conies [are] a people not strong, And they place in a rock their house,

30.he: מֶ֭לֶךְ אֵ֣ין לָאַרְבֶּ֑ה וַיֵּצֵ֖א חֹצֵ֣ץ כֻּלּֽוֹ׃

lines.text: The locusts have no king, yet they advance in ranks.
A king there is not to the locust, And it goeth out — each one shouting,

30.he: שְׂ֭מָמִית בְּיָדַ֣יִם תְּתַפֵּ֑שׂ וְ֝הִ֗יא בְּהֵ֣יכְלֵי מֶֽלֶךְ׃

lines.text: You can catch a lizard with your hands, yet it is in kings’ palaces.
A spider with two hands taketh hold, And is in the palaces of a king.

30.he: שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה הֵ֭מָּה מֵיטִ֣יבֵי צָ֑עַד וְ֝אַרְבָּעָ֗ה מֵיטִ֥בֵי לָֽכֶת׃

lines.text: “There are three things which are stately in their march, four which are stately in going:
Three there are going well, Yea, four are good in going:

30.he: לַ֭יִשׁ גִּבּ֣וֹר בַּבְּהֵמָ֑ה וְלֹא־יָ֝שׁ֗וּב מִפְּנֵי־כֹֽל׃

lines.text: The lion, which is mightiest among animals, and doesn’t turn away for any;
An old lion — mighty among beasts, That turneth not back from the face of any,

30.he: זַרְזִ֣יר מָתְנַ֣יִם אוֹ־תָ֑יִשׁ וּ֝מֶ֗לֶךְ אַלְק֥וּם עִמּֽוֹ׃

lines.text: the greyhound; the male goat; and the king against whom there is no rising up.
A girt one of the loins, or a he-goat, And a king — no rising up with him.

30.he: אִם־נָבַ֥לְתָּ בְהִתְנַשֵּׂ֑א וְאִם־זַ֝מּ֗וֹתָ יָ֣ד לְפֶֽה׃

lines.text: “If you have done foolishly in lifting up yourself, or if you have thought evil, put your hand over your mouth.
If thou hast been foolish in lifting up thyself, And if thou hast devised evil — hand to mouth!

30.he: כִּ֤י מִ֪יץ חָלָ֡ב י֘וֹצִ֤יא חֶמְאָ֗ה וּֽמִיץ־אַ֭ף י֣וֹצִיא דָ֑ם וּמִ֥יץ אַ֝פַּ֗יִם י֣וֹצִיא רִֽיב׃

lines.text: For as the churning of milk produces butter, and the wringing of the nose produces blood; so the forcing of wrath produces strife.”
For the churning of milk bringeth out butter, And the wringing of the nose bringeth out blood, And the forcing of anger bringeth out strife!

31.he: דִּ֭בְרֵי לְמוּאֵ֣ל מֶ֑לֶךְ מַ֝שָּׂ֗א אֲֽשֶׁר־יִסְּרַ֥תּוּ אִמּֽוֹ׃

lines.text: The words of king Lemuel; the revelation which his mother taught him.
Words of Lemuel a king, a declaration that his mother taught him:

31.he: מַה־בְּ֭רִי וּמַֽה־בַּר־בִּטְנִ֑י וּ֝מֶה בַּר־נְדָרָֽי׃

lines.text: “Oh, my son! Oh, son of my womb! Oh, son of my vows!
'What, my son? and what, son of my womb? And what, son of my vows?

31.he: אַל־תִּתֵּ֣ן לַנָּשִׁ֣ים חֵילֶ֑ךָ וּ֝דְרָכֶ֗יךָ לַֽמְח֥וֹת מְלָכִֽין׃

lines.text: Don’t give your strength to women, nor your ways to that which destroys kings.
Give not to women thy strength, And thy ways to wiping away of kings.

31.he: אַ֤ל לַֽמְלָכִ֨ים ׀ לְֽמוֹאֵ֗ל אַ֣ל לַֽמְלָכִ֣ים שְׁתוֹ־יָ֑יִן וּ֝לְרוֹזְנִ֗ים או שֵׁכָֽר׃

lines.text: It is not for kings, Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine, nor for princes to say, ‘Where is strong drink?’
Not for kings, O Lemuel, Not for kings, to drink wine, And for princes a desire of strong drink.

31.he: פֶּן־יִ֭שְׁתֶּה וְיִשְׁכַּ֣ח מְחֻקָּ֑ק וִֽ֝ישַׁנֶּה דִּ֣ין כָּל־בְּנֵי־עֹֽנִי׃

lines.text: lest they drink, and forget the law, and pervert the justice due to anyone who is afflicted.
Lest he drink, and forget the decree, And change the judgment of any of the sons of affliction.

31.he: תְּנוּ־שֵׁכָֽר לְאוֹבֵ֑ד וְ֝יַיִן לְמָ֣רֵי נָֽפֶשׁ׃

lines.text: Give strong drink to him who is ready to perish, and wine to the bitter in soul.
Give strong drink to the perishing, And wine to the bitter in soul,

31.he: יִ֭שְׁתֶּה וְיִשְׁכַּ֣ח רִישׁ֑וֹ וַ֝עֲמָל֗וֹ לֹ֣א יִזְכָּר־עֽוֹד׃

lines.text: Let him drink, and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more.
He drinketh, and forgetteth his poverty, And his misery he remembereth not again.

31.he: פְּתַח־פִּ֥יךָ לְאִלֵּ֑ם אֶל־דִּ֝֗ין כָּל־בְּנֵ֥י חֲלֽוֹף׃

lines.text: Open your mouth for the mute, in the cause of all who are left desolate.
Open thy mouth for the dumb, For the right of all sons of change.

31.he: פְּתַח־פִּ֥יךָ שְׁפָט־צֶ֑דֶק וְ֝דִ֗ין עָנִ֥י וְאֶבְיֽוֹן׃

lines.text: Open your mouth, judge righteously, and serve justice to the poor and needy.”
Open thy mouth, judge righteously, Both the cause of the poor and needy!'

31.he: אֵֽשֶׁת־חַ֭יִל מִ֣י יִמְצָ֑א וְרָחֹ֖ק מִפְּנִינִ֣ים מִכְרָֽהּ׃

lines.text: Who can find a worthy woman? For her price is far above rubies.
A woman of worth who doth find? Yea, far above rubies [is] her price.

31.he: בָּ֣טַח בָּ֭הּ לֵ֣ב בַּעְלָ֑הּ וְ֝שָׁלָ֗ל לֹ֣א יֶחְסָֽר׃

lines.text: The heart of her husband trusts in her. He shall have no lack of gain.
The heart of her husband hath trusted in her, And spoil he lacketh not.

31.he: גְּמָלַ֣תְהוּ ט֣וֹב וְלֹא־רָ֑ע כֹּ֝֗ל יְמֵ֣י חַיֶּֽיה׃

lines.text: She does him good, and not harm, all the days of her life.
She hath done him good, and not evil, All days of her life.

31.he: דָּ֭רְשָׁה צֶ֣מֶר וּפִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַ֝תַּ֗עַשׂ בְּחֵ֣פֶץ כַּפֶּֽיהָ׃

lines.text: She seeks wool and flax, and works eagerly with her hands.
She hath sought wool and flax, And with delight she worketh [with] her hands.

31.he: הָ֭יְתָה כָּאֳנִיּ֣וֹת סוֹחֵ֑ר מִ֝מֶּרְחָ֗ק תָּבִ֥יא לַחְמָֽהּ׃

lines.text: She is like the merchant ships. She brings her bread from afar.
She hath been as ships of the merchant, From afar she bringeth in her bread.

31.he: וַתָּ֤קָם ׀ בְּע֬וֹד לַ֗יְלָה וַתִּתֵּ֣ן טֶ֣רֶף לְבֵיתָ֑הּ וְ֝חֹ֗ק לְנַעֲרֹתֶֽיהָ׃

lines.text: She rises also while it is yet night, gives food to her household, and portions for her servant girls.
Yea, she riseth while yet night, And giveth food to her household, And a portion to her damsels.

31.he: זָמְמָ֣ה שָׂ֭דֶה וַתִּקָּחֵ֑הוּ מִפְּרִ֥י כַ֝פֶּ֗יהָ נטע כָּֽרֶם׃

lines.text: She considers a field, and buys it. With the fruit of her hands, she plants a vineyard.
She hath considered a field, and taketh it, From the fruit of her hands she hath planted a vineyard.

31.he: חָֽגְרָ֣ה בְע֣וֹז מָתְנֶ֑יהָ וַ֝תְּאַמֵּ֗ץ זְרֹעוֹתֶֽיהָ׃

lines.text: She arms her waist with strength, and makes her arms strong.
She hath girded with might her loins, And doth strengthen her arms.

31.he: טָ֭עֲמָה כִּי־ט֣וֹב סַחְרָ֑הּ לֹֽא־יִכְבֶּ֖ה בליל נֵרָֽהּ׃

lines.text: She perceives that her merchandise is profitable. Her lamp doesn’t go out by night.
She hath perceived when her merchandise [is] good, Her lamp is not extinguished in the night.

31.he: יָ֭דֶיהָ שִׁלְּחָ֣ה בַכִּישׁ֑וֹר וְ֝כַפֶּ֗יהָ תָּ֣מְכוּ פָֽלֶךְ׃

lines.text: She lays her hands to the distaff, and her hands hold the spindle.
Her hands she hath sent forth on a spindle, And her hands have held a distaff.

31.he: כַּ֭פָּהּ פָּרְשָׂ֣ה לֶעָנִ֑י וְ֝יָדֶ֗יהָ שִׁלְּחָ֥ה לָֽאֶבְיֽוֹן׃

lines.text: She opens her arms to the poor; yes, she extends her hands to the needy.
Her hand she hath spread forth to the poor, Yea, her hands she sent forth to the needy.

31.he: לֹא־תִירָ֣א לְבֵיתָ֣הּ מִשָּׁ֑לֶג כִּ֥י כָל־בֵּ֝יתָ֗הּ לָבֻ֥שׁ שָׁנִֽים׃

lines.text: She is not afraid of the snow for her household; for all her household are clothed with scarlet.
She is not afraid of her household from snow, For all her household are clothed [with] scarlet.

31.he: מַרְבַדִּ֥ים עָֽשְׂתָה־לָּ֑הּ שֵׁ֖שׁ וְאַרְגָּמָ֣ן לְבוּשָֽׁהּ׃

lines.text: She makes for herself carpets of tapestry. Her clothing is fine linen and purple.
Ornamental coverings she hath made for herself, Silk and purple [are] her clothing.

31.he: נוֹדָ֣ע בַּשְּׁעָרִ֣ים בַּעְלָ֑הּ בְּ֝שִׁבְתּ֗וֹ עִם־זִקְנֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃

lines.text: Her husband is respected in the gates, when he sits among the elders of the land.
Known in the gates is her husband, In his sitting with elders of the land.

31.he: סָדִ֣ין עָ֭שְׂתָה וַתִּמְכֹּ֑ר וַ֝חֲג֗וֹר נָתְנָ֥ה לַֽכְּנַעֲנִֽי׃

lines.text: She makes linen garments and sells them, and delivers sashes to the merchant.
Linen garments she hath made, and selleth, And a girdle she hath given to the merchant.

31.he: עֹז־וְהָדָ֥ר לְבוּשָׁ֑הּ וַ֝תִּשְׂחַ֗ק לְי֣וֹם אַחֲרֽוֹן׃

lines.text: Strength and dignity are her clothing. She laughs at the time to come.
Strength and honour [are] her clothing, And she rejoiceth at a latter day.

31.he: פִּ֭יהָ פָּתְחָ֣ה בְחָכְמָ֑ה וְתֽוֹרַת־חֶ֝֗סֶד עַל־לְשׁוֹנָֽהּ׃

lines.text: She opens her mouth with wisdom. Kind instruction is on her tongue.
Her mouth she hath opened in wisdom, And the law of kindness [is] on her tongue.

31.he: צ֭וֹפִיָּה הֲלִיכ֣וֹת בֵּיתָ֑הּ וְלֶ֥חֶם עַ֝צְל֗וּת לֹ֣א תֹאכֵֽל׃

lines.text: She looks well to the ways of her household, and doesn’t eat the bread of idleness.
She [is] watching the ways of her household, And bread of sloth she eateth not.

31.he: קָ֣מוּ בָ֭נֶיהָ וַֽיְאַשְּׁר֑וּהָ בַּ֝עְלָ֗הּ וַֽיְהַֽלְלָהּ׃

lines.text: Her children rise up and call her blessed. Her husband also praises her:
Her sons have risen up, and pronounce her happy, Her husband, and he praiseth her,

31.he: רַבּ֣וֹת בָּ֭נוֹת עָ֣שׂוּ חָ֑יִל וְ֝אַ֗תְּ עָלִ֥ית עַל־כֻּלָּֽנָה׃

lines.text: “Many women do noble things, but you excel them all.”
'Many [are] the daughters who have done worthily, Thou hast gone up above them all.'

31.he: שֶׁ֣קֶר הַ֭חֵן וְהֶ֣בֶל הַיֹּ֑פִי אִשָּׁ֥ה יִרְאַת־יְ֝הוָ֗ה הִ֣יא תִתְהַלָּֽל׃

lines.text: Charm is deceitful, and beauty is vain; but a woman who fears Yahweh, she shall be praised.
The grace [is] false, and the beauty [is] vain, A woman fearing Jehovah, she may boast herself.

31.he: תְּנוּ־לָ֭הּ מִפְּרִ֣י יָדֶ֑יהָ וִֽיהַלְל֖וּהָ בַשְּׁעָרִ֣ים מַעֲשֶֽׂיהָ׃

lines.text: Give her of the fruit of her hands! Let her works praise her in the gates!
Give ye to her of the fruit of her hands, And her works do praise her in the gates!
